# Spend Limits

Cap what a personal account or a team can spend in a month or a day: the whole wallet, one team member, one API key, a surface such as the LLM gateway, or one agent.

## How Spend Limits Work

A spend limit caps what a wallet can spend in a month or a day. Limits work the same way for a personal account's wallet and for a team's wallet. The limits of the workspace a call runs in apply: a team project's API key runs in its team, a personal project's key in your personal account, and the dashboard in the workspace you have selected.

Manage limits in the dashboard under [Controls > Spend Limits](https://wiro.ai/panel/controls/spend-limits), for your personal account or for the team workspace you have selected, or with the `/SpendLimit` endpoints below. Team and member limits set before this system were moved into it as monthly limits of the same amount.

### What a Limit Caps

Each limit caps one scope of the wallet's spending:

| Scope | `target` | What it caps |
|-------|----------|--------------|
| `account` | None | The whole wallet. In a team, the whole team's spending |
| `member` | The member's `useruuid` from `/Team/Member/List` | One team member's spending in the team (team wallets only). A member's spending includes their dashboard runs in the team workspace and every run made with the API key of a team project they created |
| `project` | The project's `id` from `/Project/List` | One API key: what is spent with that project's key |
| `surface` | `web`, `api`, `mcp`, `llm-gateway`, `extension`, `agent`, `studio`, `workflow-agent` or `workflow` | One way in (see Surfaces below) |
| `agent` | The agent's `guid` (its `useragentguid`) | One deployed agent: all of its AI usage, both what its plan includes and what the balance pays, and its own model runs. Its plan payments count toward the wallet's other limits, not this one |

### Surfaces

| Surface | Label | Covers |
|---------|-------|--------|
| `web` | the dashboard | The Wiro dashboard, and calls with a signed-in user's Bearer token |
| `api` | the API | Calls with an API key, including [`/sync`](/docs/run-a-model#run-sync) and, for now, the [Wiro MCP package](/docs/mcp-self-hosted) when you run it yourself |
| `mcp` | MCP | The hosted [Wiro MCP server](/docs/wiro-mcp-server) at `mcp.wiro.ai`, and the Wiro MCP package when it names itself (see [Surfaces](/docs/tasks#task-surfaces)) |
| `llm-gateway` | the LLM gateway | The OpenAI and Anthropic compatible [LLM gateway](/docs/completions-api) at `llm.wiro.ai` |
| `extension` | the browser extensions | Only the Wiro browser extensions |
| `agent` | agents | Your deployed agents: their plan payments, the AI usage their balance pays and the models they run |
| `studio` | Studio | [Studio](/docs/studio): the messages you send it and the models it runs for you |
| `workflow-agent` | the Workflow Agent | The [Workflow Agent](/docs/workflow-agent): the messages you send it |
| `workflow` | workflows | [Workflow](/docs/workflows) runs and resumes, and every step they run |

When work fits more than one surface, the first match in this order decides: who does it (Studio, the Workflow Agent or a deployed agent), what it is (a workflow run and its steps, unless a deployed agent, Studio or the Workflow Agent started it), which client sends it (the LLM gateway, a browser extension or MCP), and last which credential it uses (an API key, else a signed-in session). So a message to Studio sent with an API key counts on `studio`, and a workflow run started with an API key or through MCP on `workflow`. Each task records the surface it counted on: see [Surfaces](/docs/tasks#task-surfaces). Refusal messages and `/SpendLimit/Usage` name a surface by its label.

Studio, the Workflow Agent and workflows used to have no surface of their own. Studio and Workflow Agent work counted on `web`, or on `api` when it was sent with an API key, and a workflow run counted on the surface that started it. Limits that were already set were not changed, so a limit on `web` or `api` no longer covers this work: to cap it by surface, set a limit on `studio`, `workflow-agent` or `workflow`.

### Periods and Amounts

A limit's `period` is `month` (the default), which resets on the 1st of each month at 00:00 UTC, or `day`, which resets every day at 00:00 UTC. A scope and target can have one monthly limit and one daily limit.

`amountusd` is the limit in USD, rounded to cents. Once rounded, it must be at least `0.01`. A limit counts everything spent in its current period, also what was spent before the limit was added, so a new limit below that amount is used up at once.

### What Counts

Every charge to the wallet for usage counts: model runs, workflow runs, realtime sessions, Studio, the Workflow Agent, agent plans and upgrades, and the AI usage of an agent that the balance pays. Deposits are not spending.

The models Studio runs for you are checked and counted like the runs you start yourself: against the account's or the team's limits, your member limit in a team, the limit of the turn's project (the API key you sent the message with, or the workspace's [Studio project](/docs/studio#costs) for a message sent from wiro.ai) and the limit of the `studio` surface. What the chat of Studio and the Workflow Agent costs counts toward your limits too, on the `studio` and `workflow-agent` surfaces.

An agent's AI usage counts in two ways. What its plan's included usage covers counts only toward the agent's own limit: the plan payment already counted toward the wallet's limits. What the balance pays once the included usage is used up counts toward the agent's own limit, the account's or the team's limit and the limit of the `agent` surface. Member and API key limits don't apply to an agent's AI usage. The models an agent runs count like any other model run, and toward the agent's own limit too.

### When Limits Are Checked

Limits are checked before work starts:

- Model runs, workflow runs and workflow resumes, and each step of a workflow run before the step starts
- Studio and Workflow Agent messages, and the models Studio runs for you
- An agent deploy, upgrade or renewal that a person starts
- Messages to an agent, against that agent's own limit and, once its plan's included usage is used up, against the account's or the team's limit and the limit of the `agent` surface

When the price of the work is known before it starts, as for fixed-price models, workflow runs and agent plans, the work is refused if spending so far, plus what work in progress holds, plus that price would go over the limit. Otherwise it is refused once the limit has no room left.

Work that is already running finishes and is charged, with two exceptions. A realtime session ends after the turn that uses up a limit, the same way it ends when the balance runs out: its WebSocket clients get a `task_session_stopped` event with `reason` `spend_limit`, code `93` and the refusal `/Run` would give (see [Realtime Voice](/docs/realtime-voice-conversation#realtime-end-session)). An agent's voice call is a realtime session too and ends the same way: a web voice call then gets `session_end` with `reason` `spend_limit` (see [Web Voice](/docs/integration-webvoice-skills#websocket-protocol)), and a caller on the phone hears a short notice before the call ends. An agent pauses at its next model call when a limit that covers it is used up, even in the middle of a reply (see below).

Every agent plan payment, a deploy, a move to a higher plan or a renewal, counts toward the account's or the team's limit and the limit of the `agent` surface, whichever way it was made, and in a team toward the limit of the member who bought the plan. A payment made with an API key also counts toward that key's limit. A plan payment never counts toward the agent's own limit. Automatic monthly renewals of running agents count the same way, with no API key, and are never refused by a limit.

### Work in Progress

A run that starts holds its expected price against every limit that covers it, until it is charged or ends. The next check counts what is held, so runs started at the same time can pass a limit by one run at most. A run whose price is not known before it starts goes ahead while the limit has room. Refusal messages show what is held, and so does `heldusd` on the limits of `/SpendLimit/List` and in `/SpendLimit/Usage`.

### When a Limit Is Reached

New work the limit covers is refused with HTTP `200`, `result: false` and error code `93`. The message names the limit and says when it resets:

```json
{
  "result": false,
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 93,
      "message": "This API key's monthly spend limit is reached ($50.20 of $50.00). It resets on December 1, 2026 at 00:00 UTC."
    }
  ]
}
```

When the price of the work is known before it starts, the message says what is left instead, for example `This team's monthly spend limit has $3.10 left of $500.00, and this run costs $4.00. It resets on December 1, 2026 at 00:00 UTC.` A daily limit says `daily` instead of `monthly`, and its message ends with `It resets at 00:00 UTC.` When work in progress holds part of the limit, the message also says how much.

| Limit | The message starts with |
|-------|-------------------------|
| A personal account's `account` limit | `Your monthly spend limit` |
| A team's `account` limit | `This team's monthly spend limit` |
| `member` | `Your monthly spend limit in this team` |
| `project` | `This API key's monthly spend limit` |
| `surface` | `The monthly spend limit for` and the surface's label, for example `The monthly spend limit for the LLM gateway` or `The monthly spend limit for the Workflow Agent` |
| `agent` | `This agent's monthly spend limit` |

Nothing runs and nothing is charged. Retrying does not help until the limit resets or someone who manages it raises it. Through the [LLM gateway](/docs/completions-api#gateway-errors) the refusal is an HTTP `402` error with code `spend_limit_reached`, and the [MCP server](/docs/wiro-mcp-server) returns it as a tool error.

When a limit that covers an agent is used up, the agent pauses: its own limit at any time, and the account's or the team's limit or the `agent` surface's limit once its plan's included usage is used up. While included usage is left, those wallet limits don't stop it. A turn that is running stops at its next model call (see [Failed turns](/docs/agent-messaging#failed-turns)), new messages to the agent are refused, and its Scheduled Tasks are paused rather than failed. In Telegram, Slack and Discord it tells people so in a plain sentence, with the time the limit resets when that is known. Once the limit resets, is raised or is removed, the agent answers again and each Scheduled Task runs at its next scheduled time, with no restart.

### Alert Emails

A limit sends an alert email when spending reaches its `alertpct`: 50, 80 (the default) or 90 percent of the limit, or `null` for no alert email. It sends a used-up email when the limit is reached. Each email goes out once per limit and period, and changing the limit re-arms both for the current period. The emails link to the Spend Limits page of the workspace the limit belongs to.

A personal account's limits email the account. A team's limits email the team's admins and the organization owner, and also the member a member limit is for, the person who created the API key a key limit is for, and the owner of the agent an agent limit is for.

### Who Can Change Limits

- **Personal account**: its owner
- **Team**: a team admin or the organization owner. The person who created the team is one of its admins

Every team member can read the team's limits and spending with `/SpendLimit/List` and `/SpendLimit/Usage`. A member who is not an admin can't change any limit: not their own member limit, and not the limits of the API keys they created or the agents they deployed. A deployed agent's own calls to the `/SpendLimit` endpoints are refused with HTTP `403`, reads included.

### Changing Limits With the API

`/SpendLimit/Set`, `/SpendLimit/Remove` and `/SpendLimit/Preview` work in the dashboard, with a signed-in user's Bearer token and with an API key:

- **With an API key**, the call acts as the person who created the key's project, in that project's workspace: the creator's personal account for a personal project, the team for a team project. The key follows its creator's current role: while the creator is a team member who is not an admin, the key can read limits but not change them.
- **With a Bearer token**, the call acts as you, in your personal account. To work in a team, send the team's guid in the `x-team-guid` header. A call whose `x-team-guid` names a team you are not a member of, and whose organization you don't own, is refused with `You are not a member of this team.` Calls with an API key ignore this header.

`/SpendLimit/List` and `/SpendLimit/Preview` return the `workspace` they work in, so you can check where a change lands before you make it. Changes made with API keys are limited to 60 per workspace in any hour, counting spend limits and Model Access rules together. Preview does not count. Each change is recorded with who made it and how.

## **POST** /SpendLimit/List

Returns the spend limits of the call's workspace, each with what has been spent in its current period, and how the call itself counts. A team project's API key reads its team, a personal project's key your personal account, and the dashboard the workspace you have selected (see [Changing Limits With the API](#changing-limits-with-the-api)). Any team member can call it, and it works with an API key. Send an empty body: `{}`.

```json
      "createdat": 1794474300,
      "updatedat": 1794474300,
      "updatedby": { "useruuid": "7a1b2c3d-4e5f-4a6b-8c7d-9e0f1a2b3c4d", "label": "John Doe" },
      "spentusd": 88.2
    }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `workspace.type` | `team` or `personal` |
| `workspace.teamguid` | The team's guid, or `null` for a personal account |
| `workspace.canmanage` | Whether the caller can change limits in this workspace: `true` for a personal account's owner, a team admin and the organization owner, also with the API key of a project they created; `false` for other team members and their keys |
| `caller.surface` | The surface this call counts on, such as `api` for a call with an API key (see [Surfaces](#how-spend-limits-work)) |
| `caller.projectid` | The project id of the API key the call used, or `null` without a key |
| `limits[].guid` | The limit's guid, for `/SpendLimit/Remove` |
| `limits[].scope` | `account`, `member`, `project`, `surface` or `agent` |
| `limits[].target` | The member's `useruuid`, the project id, the surface or the agent's guid; `""` for `account` |
| `limits[].targetlabel` | The member's name, the project's name, the agent's title or the surface's label; `null` for `account` |
| `limits[].period` | `month` or `day` |
| `limits[].amountusd` | The limit in USD |
| `limits[].alertpct` | `50`, `80` or `90`, or `null` for no alert email |
| `limits[].periodstart` | Start of the current period, in Unix seconds |
| `limits[].resetsat` | When the current period ends and the limit resets, in Unix seconds |
| `limits[].createdat`, `limits[].updatedat` | When the limit was added and last changed, in Unix seconds |
| `limits[].updatedby` | Who changed the limit last: `useruuid` and `label`, the person's name, or their email when they have no name. In a team, the owner of its organization who is not a member of the team is labeled `the organization owner`, and someone who has left the team has a `null` label. A change made with an API key names the person who created the key's project. `updatedby` is `null` when Wiro changed the limit last, as for the team and member limits moved into this system |
| `limits[].spentusd` | What has been spent in the current period, in USD |
| `limits[].heldusd` | When work in progress holds part of the limit: how much it holds, in USD (see [Work in Progress](#work-in-progress)) |

## **POST** /SpendLimit/Set

Adds a spend limit to the call's workspace, or changes the existing limit with the same `scope`, `target` and `period`. Changing a limit re-arms its emails for the current period. Only the people who can change limits can call it (see [Who Can Change Limits](#who-can-change-limits)), in the dashboard, with a Bearer token or with an API key. To check a change first, send the same body to [`/SpendLimit/Preview`](#spend-limit-preview).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `scope` | string | Yes | `"account"`, `"member"`, `"project"`, `"surface"` or `"agent"`. See [Spend Limits](#how-spend-limits-work) |
| `target` | string | For every scope but `account` | The member's `useruuid`, the project's `id`, the surface (`web`, `api`, `mcp`, `llm-gateway`, `extension`, `agent`, `studio`, `workflow-agent` or `workflow`) or the agent's guid. Leave it out for `account` |
| `period` | string | No | `"month"` or `"day"`. Default: `"month"` |
| `amountusd` | number | Yes | The limit in USD, rounded to cents. Once rounded, it must be at least `0.01` |
| `alertpct` | number | No | When the alert email goes out: `50`, `80` or `90` percent of the limit, or `null` for no alert email. Default: `80` |

### Examples

**Cap the whole wallet at $500 a month, with the alert at 90%:**

```json
{
  "scope": "account",
  "amountusd": 500,
  "alertpct": 90
}
```

**Cap one API key at $100 a month:**

```json
{
  "scope": "project",
  "target": "48211",
  "period": "month",
  "amountusd": 100
}
```

**Cap the LLM gateway at $25 a day, with no alert email:**

```json
{
  "scope": "surface",
  "target": "llm-gateway",
  "period": "day",
  "amountusd": 25,
  "alertpct": null
}
```

`limit` is the limit as saved, shaped like a row of `/SpendLimit/List`:

```json
// Response
{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "limit": {
    "guid": "15be7fb3-c602-4ff1-a3f1-3afaa3996974",
    "scope": "project",
    "target": "48211",
    "targetlabel": "Production",
    "period": "month",
    "amountusd": 100,
    "alertpct": 80,
    "periodstart": 1793491200,
    "resetsat": 1796083200,
    "createdat": 1794474300,
    "updatedat": 1794474300,
    "updatedby": { "useruuid": "7a1b2c3d-4e5f-4a6b-8c7d-9e0f1a2b3c4d", "label": "John Doe" },
    "spentusd": 61.4
  }
}
```

### Errors

| Error | Cause |
|-------|-------|
| `scope must be one of account, member, project, surface, agent.` | `scope` is missing or not one of the five scopes |
| `Member limits exist only in a team workspace.` | A `member` limit in a personal account |
| `target is required for this scope.` | No `target` for a `member`, `project`, `surface` or `agent` limit |
| `A surface is one of web, api, mcp, llm-gateway, extension, agent, studio, workflow-agent, workflow.` | A `surface` limit with another `target` |
| `target must be a project id.` | A `project` limit whose `target` is not a project id |
| `period must be month or day.` | Another `period` |
| `amountusd must be a positive number.` | `amountusd` is missing, zero or negative |
| `amountusd is too large.` | `amountusd` is over 10,000,000 |
| `amountusd must be at least 0.01.` | `amountusd` is above zero but rounds to less than one cent |
| `alertpct must be 50, 80 or 90, or null for no alert.` | Another `alertpct` |
| `You are not a member of this team.` | With a Bearer token, `x-team-guid` names a team you are not a member of, and whose organization you don't own |
| `Only a team admin or the organization owner can change this limit.` | In a team, a signed-in caller is not a team admin or the organization owner |
| `This API key acts as the person who created it, who is a member of this team. Only a team admin or the organization owner can change this limit.` | With an API key, the person who created the key's project is a team member who is not an admin |
| `That person is not an active member of this team.` | A `member` limit for someone who is not an active member of the team |
| `That API key's project is not in this workspace.` | A `project` limit for a project of another workspace |
| `That agent is not in this workspace.` | An `agent` limit for an agent of another workspace |
| `Too many changes to Spend Limits and Model Access in the last hour. Try again later.` | With API keys, this workspace's spend limits and Model Access rules have been changed 60 times in the last hour |

## **POST** /SpendLimit/Preview

Shows what `/SpendLimit/Set` would do, and changes nothing. It takes the same body as `/SpendLimit/Set` and checks it the same way, so only the people who can change limits can call it. Use it to see which workspace a change lands in, the limit as it would be saved and the limit it would replace.

### Example

**Raise the Production API key's monthly limit to $150:**

```json
{
  "scope": "project",
  "target": "48211",
  "period": "month",
  "amountusd": 150
}
```

```json
// Response
{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "preview": true,
  "workspace": {
    "type": "team",
    "teamguid": "0d9aade4-d31b-4b97-88f3-a90482f080ea",
    "canmanage": true
  },
  "limit": {
    "guid": "15be7fb3-c602-4ff1-a3f1-3afaa3996974",
    "scope": "project",
    "target": "48211",
    "targetlabel": "Production",
    "period": "month",
    "amountusd": 150,
    "alertpct": 80,
    "periodstart": 1793491200,
    "resetsat": 1796083200,
    "createdat": 1794474300,
    "updatedat": null,
    "updatedby": null,
    "spentusd": 88.2
  },
  "existing": {
    "guid": "15be7fb3-c602-4ff1-a3f1-3afaa3996974",
    "scope": "project",
    "target": "48211",
    "targetlabel": "Production",
    "period": "month",
    "amountusd": 100,
    "alertpct": 80,
    "periodstart": 1793491200,
    "resetsat": 1796083200,
    "createdat": 1794474300,
    "updatedat": 1794474300,
    "updatedby": { "useruuid": "7a1b2c3d-4e5f-4a6b-8c7d-9e0f1a2b3c4d", "label": "John Doe" },
    "spentusd": 88.2
  }
}
```

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `preview` | Always `true`: nothing was changed |
| `workspace` | The workspace the change would be made in, as in `/SpendLimit/List`: `type`, `teamguid` and `canmanage`, which is always `true` here |
| `limit` | The limit as `/SpendLimit/Set` would save it, shaped like a row of `/SpendLimit/List`, with what has been spent in its current period. Its `guid` and `createdat` are those of the limit it would replace, or `null` for a new limit, and its `updatedat` and `updatedby` are `null` |
| `existing` | The current limit with the same `scope`, `target` and `period`, which the change would replace, or `null` when there is none |

When `limit.spentusd` is already at or above the new amount, the limit is used up as soon as it is saved. The errors are those of `/SpendLimit/Set`, except that Preview does not count toward the hourly cap on changes made with API keys.

## **POST** /SpendLimit/Remove

Removes a spend limit from the call's workspace. The people who can change limits can remove one, in the dashboard, with a Bearer token or with an API key.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `guid` | string | Yes | The limit's `guid` from `/SpendLimit/List` |

```json
// Response
{
  "result": true,
  "errors": []
}
```

| Error | Cause |
|-------|-------|
| `guid is required.` | No `guid` was sent |
| `Limit not found in this workspace.` | The guid is not a limit of the call's workspace, or it was already removed |
| `You are not a member of this team.` | With a Bearer token, `x-team-guid` names a team you are not a member of, and whose organization you don't own |
| `Only a team admin or the organization owner can change this limit.` | In a team, a signed-in caller is not a team admin or the organization owner |
| `This API key acts as the person who created it, who is a member of this team. Only a team admin or the organization owner can change this limit.` | With an API key, the person who created the key's project is a team member who is not an admin |
| `Too many changes to Spend Limits and Model Access in the last hour. Try again later.` | With API keys, this workspace's spend limits and Model Access rules have been changed 60 times in the last hour |

## **POST** /SpendLimit/Usage

Returns what the call's workspace has spent this month or today, in total and by surface, member, API key and agent. A team project's API key reads its team, a personal project's key your personal account, and the dashboard the workspace you have selected. Any team member can call it, and it works with an API key.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `period` | string | No | `"month"` or `"day"`. Default: `"month"` |

```json
// Response
{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "usage": {
    "period": "month",
    "periodstart": 1793491200,
    "resetsat": 1796083200,
    "totalusd": 248.7,
    "heldusd": 3.5,
    "surfaces": [
      { "surface": "web", "label": "the dashboard", "spentusd": 21.4 },
      { "surface": "api", "label": "the API", "spentusd": 168.2, "heldusd": 3.5 },
      { "surface": "mcp", "label": "MCP", "spentusd": 12.5 },
      { "surface": "llm-gateway", "label": "the LLM gateway", "spentusd": 7.9 },
      { "surface": "extension", "label": "the browser extensions", "spentusd": 0 },
      { "surface": "agent", "label": "agents", "spentusd": 20 },
      { "surface": "studio", "label": "Studio", "spentusd": 14.5 },
      { "surface": "workflow-agent", "label": "the Workflow Agent", "spentusd": 0.8 },
      { "surface": "workflow", "label": "workflows", "spentusd": 3.4 }
    ],
    "members": [
      { "useruuid": "3f5a9c20-6d41-4b8e-a1c7-5e9d0f2b4c61", "label": "Jane Doe", "spentusd": 120.5 },
      { "useruuid": "7a1b2c3d-4e5f-4a6b-8c7d-9e0f1a2b3c4d", "label": "John Doe", "spentusd": 108.2, "heldusd": 3.5 }
    ],
    "projects": [
      { "projectid": "48211", "label": "Production", "spentusd": 88.2 },
      { "projectid": "48377", "label": "Staging", "spentusd": 80, "heldusd": 3.5 }
    ],
    "agents": [
      { "useragentguid": "6e4bbd6f-6b73-4421-adae-e9599ba2e317", "label": "Support Agent", "spentusd": 20 }
    ]
  }
}
```

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `usage.period` | `month` or `day` |
| `usage.periodstart`, `usage.resetsat` | Start and end of the period, in Unix seconds |
| `usage.totalusd` | What the wallet has spent in the period, in USD |
| `usage.heldusd` | What work in progress holds, in USD. Present only when it holds something (see [Work in Progress](#work-in-progress)) |
| `usage.surfaces` | One row per surface, always all nine in the order `web`, `api`, `mcp`, `llm-gateway`, `extension`, `agent`, `studio`, `workflow-agent`, `workflow`, with its label |
| `usage.members` | Spending per team member, with the member's name as `label`. Empty for a personal account |
| `usage.projects` | Spending per API key, with the project's name as `label` |
| `usage.agents` | Spending per deployed agent, with the agent's title as `label` |
| `heldusd` in a row of `usage.surfaces`, `usage.members`, `usage.projects` or `usage.agents` | What work in progress holds for that row, present only when it holds something. A member, API key or agent whose only spending so far is held work is listed with `spentusd` `0` |

An agent plan's automatic renewal counts in `totalusd`, in the `agent` row of `usage.surfaces` and, in a team, in the row of the member who bought the plan, but in no row of `usage.projects` or `usage.agents`, so those rows can add up to less than `totalusd`. An agent's row counts what its own limit counts, so it also holds the AI usage its plan covered, which is not in `totalusd`: the plan payment already is.

For other breakdowns, `/Project/UsageSummary` gives usage per project and `/Task/Stat` gives time-series task execution data. Both filter by the active workspace.

# Model Access

Choose which models a personal account or a team can run: allow or block single models and whole categories, for the whole wallet, one team member, one API key, a surface such as the LLM gateway, or one agent.

## How Model Access Works

A Model Access rule decides which models a wallet's work can run. Rules work the same way for a personal account's wallet and for a team's wallet. The rules of the workspace a call runs in apply: a team project's API key runs in its team, a personal project's key in your personal account, and the dashboard in the workspace you have selected.

Manage rules in the dashboard under [Controls > Model Access](https://wiro.ai/panel/controls/model-access), for your personal account or for the team workspace you have selected, or with the `/ModelAccess` endpoints below. A workspace without rules can run every model. Team allowlists and blocklists set before this system were moved into it as rules for the whole team.

### What a Rule Covers

Each rule covers one scope of the wallet's work, the same scopes as [spend limits](/docs/spend-limits). A scope and target can have one rule:

| Scope | `target` | What it covers |
|-------|----------|----------------|
| `account` | None | Everything the wallet runs. In a team, every run in the team |
| `member` | The member's `useruuid` from `/Team/Member/List` | One team member's runs in the team (team wallets only): their dashboard runs in the team workspace and every run made with the API key of a team project they created |
| `project` | The project's `id` from `/Project/List` | One API key: the runs made with that project's key |
| `surface` | `web`, `api`, `mcp`, `llm-gateway`, `extension`, `agent`, `studio`, `workflow-agent` or `workflow` | One way in (see Surfaces below) |
| `agent` | The agent's `guid` (its `useragentguid`) | One deployed agent: the models it runs through Wiro, the chat models it answers with and its built-in voice |

### Surfaces

| Surface | Covers |
|---------|--------|
| `web` | The Wiro dashboard, and calls with a signed-in user's Bearer token |
| `api` | Calls with an API key, including [`/sync`](/docs/run-a-model#run-sync) and, for now, the [Wiro MCP package](/docs/mcp-self-hosted) when you run it yourself |
| `mcp` | The hosted [Wiro MCP server](/docs/wiro-mcp-server) at `mcp.wiro.ai`, and the Wiro MCP package when it names itself (see [Surfaces](/docs/tasks#task-surfaces)) |
| `llm-gateway` | The OpenAI and Anthropic compatible [LLM gateway](/docs/completions-api) at `llm.wiro.ai` |
| `extension` | Only the Wiro browser extensions |
| `agent` | Your deployed agents' own runs |
| `studio` | [Studio](/docs/studio): the chat model of each message you send it, and the models it runs for you |
| `workflow-agent` | The [Workflow Agent](/docs/workflow-agent): the chat model of each message you send it |
| `workflow` | [Workflow](/docs/workflows) runs and resumes, and every step they run |

A run counts on one surface, decided the same way as for [spend limits](/docs/spend-limits): the first match among who does it (Studio, the Workflow Agent or a deployed agent), what it is (a workflow run and its steps, unless a deployed agent, Studio or the Workflow Agent started it), which client sends it (the LLM gateway, a browser extension or MCP), and last which credential it uses (an API key, else a signed-in session). So a message to Studio sent with an API key counts on `studio`, and a workflow run started with an API key or through MCP on `workflow`. See [Surfaces](/docs/tasks#task-surfaces).

Studio, the Workflow Agent and workflows used to have no surface of their own. Studio and Workflow Agent work counted on `web`, or on `api` when it was sent with an API key, and a workflow run counted on the surface that started it. Rules that were already set were not changed, so a rule on `web` or `api` no longer covers this work: to decide its models by surface, set a rule on `studio`, `workflow-agent` or `workflow`.

### Everything Else

Every rule has an Everything Else setting, `access`. It decides the models the rule names neither one by one nor by category:

- `allow` (the default): every model can run except the ones the rule blocks
- `block`: only the models and categories the rule allows can run

### Categories

A rule can allow or block whole categories of models. Each category groups catalog categories, the values models carry in their `categories` field on [`/Tool/List` and `/Tool/Detail`](/docs/models). A category also covers the models added to it later.

| `category` | Label | Catalog categories |
|------------|-------|--------------------|
| `image` | Image Generation | `text-to-image`, `image-to-image`, `image-editing`, `image-to-text` |
| `video` | Video Generation | `text-to-video`, `image-to-video`, `video-to-video`, `speech-to-video`, `talking-head`, `video-to-text`, `reference-to-video`, `audio-to-video`, `lip-sync` |
| `audio` | Audio & Speech | `text-to-speech`, `speech-to-text`, `speech-to-speech`, `video-to-music`, `voice-clone`, `text-to-audio`, `image-to-audio`, `realtime-conversation`, `realtime-tts`, `realtime-stt` |
| `music` | Music Generation | `music-generation`, `text-to-song`, `text-to-music`, `image-to-song`, `image-to-music` |
| `3d` | 3D Generation | `3d-generation`, `text-to-3d`, `image-to-3d` |
| `llm` | LLM & Chat | `chat`, `llm`, `partner-llm`, `rag`, `llm-reasoning` |
| `utilities` | Utilities | `utils` |

A model is in every category that one of its catalog categories belongs to, so it can be in more than one. A model whose catalog categories belong to none of them is decided by its own entry or by Everything Else. `/ModelAccess/List` returns this list, and `/ModelAccess/Check` shows the categories of one model.

### Single Models

A rule can also allow or block single models, named by their `owner/slug`, such as `openai/gpt-6-2-astra`, or by their `id`. A model's own entry comes before its categories, so a rule can block a category and still allow one model in it. A rule can name up to 500 models, and each must be a model listed on Wiro.

### How One Rule Decides

A rule decides a model in this order:

1. **The model**: when the rule names the model, that entry decides
2. **Its categories**: otherwise, when the rule names one or more of the model's categories, they decide. If one of them is blocked, the model is blocked, even when another one is allowed
3. **Everything Else**: otherwise the rule's `access` decides

For example, a rule with Everything Else set to `allow`, Video Generation blocked and `bytedance/seedance-v2-5-flash` allowed lets every model run except video models, and Seedance v2.5 Flash is the one video model it lets run.

### When Several Rules Apply

A run can meet several rules of its wallet: the whole account's, the member's in a team, the API key's, the surface's and the agent's. It goes ahead only when every rule that applies allows the model. A narrower rule can't open what a wider one blocks: when the account's rule blocks a model, an API key's rule that allows it does not let it run.

When more than one rule blocks the model, the refusal names the first of them in the order account, member, API key, surface, agent. `/ModelAccess/Check` shows how each rule decides a model.

### Where Rules Apply

Rules are checked before work starts:

- Model runs: `/Run` and its `/sync` wait, realtime sessions, the [LLM gateway](/docs/completions-api), the [MCP server](/docs/wiro-mcp-server), the browser extensions and the dashboard
- Workflow runs and resumes: every model step that will run must be allowed. Steps that will not run, such as the steps after a breakpoint, are not checked
- Studio and the Workflow Agent: the models Studio runs for you, and the chat model of each message you send to Studio or the Workflow Agent, follow your own rules like the runs you start yourself: the account's or the team's rule, your member rule in a team, the rule of the turn's project (the API key you sent the message with, or the workspace's [Studio project](/docs/studio#costs) for a message sent from wiro.ai) and the rule of the `studio` surface, or of `workflow-agent` for a message to the Workflow Agent. A message whose chat model a rule blocks, the `model` it names or the default chat model when it names none, is refused with code `92` before anything runs. Chat models are LLM & Chat models: a rule that blocks LLM & Chat blocks them unless it allows the chat model by name, and a rule that lets only selected models run blocks them unless it allows LLM & Chat or the chat model. The Workflow Agent runs nothing but its chat model. [`/Studio/Status`](/docs/studio#post-studiostatus) and [`/StudioWorkflow/Status`](/docs/workflow-agent#post-studioworkflowstatus) list the chat models your rules block
- The models your deployed agents run through Wiro
- An agent's chat model: choosing one in the agent's settings, or sending `model` with `Message/Send`, follows that agent's own rule, the account's or the team's rule and the rule of the `agent` surface, since the agent's AI usage past its plan is paid from the wallet. Member and API key rules don't apply to it. If one of these rules blocks the model the agent already uses, its model calls are refused and the turn ends with `[MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED]`. A Scheduled Task whose model a rule blocks is paused rather than failed, and runs again at its next scheduled time once the model is allowed or another one is chosen
- An agent's built-in voice: transcription of the voice notes people send the agent, and the voice replies it sends, follow the same rules as its chat model, as Audio & Speech models. A rule that blocks Audio & Speech, or that lets only selected models run without allowing Audio & Speech, blocks them, even when it allows LLM & Chat. Voice notes are then not transcribed, and the agent replies in text. An agent that chats on a Gemini model has its voice notes transcribed by `google/gemini-3-flash`, so a rule that names that model decides them too. A rule that does not name that model blocks those voice notes unless it lets both Audio & Speech and LLM & Chat models run

A change applies to work that starts after it. Work that is already running is not stopped, and a deployed agent's chat model and voice follow a change within about a minute. Browsing models is not affected: `/Tool/List`, `/Tool/Detail` and the LLM gateway's model list show the same models whatever the rules.

### When a Model Is Blocked

A run of a model that a rule blocks is refused with HTTP `200`, `result: false` and error code `92`, even when the wallet has money. The message names the rule:

```json
{
  "result": false,
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 92,
      "message": "This API key can only use selected models, and openai/gpt-6-2-astra is not one of them. Model Access rules decide which models can run."
    }
  ]
}
```

The message also says what blocked the model:

| Blocked by | Example message |
|------------|-----------------|
| Everything Else | `This API key can only use selected models, and openai/gpt-6-2-astra is not one of them. Model Access rules decide which models can run.` |
| The model's own entry | `This API key can't use openai/gpt-6-2-astra. Model Access rules decide which models can run.` |
| One of the model's categories | `MCP can't use Video Generation models, and bytedance/seedance-v2-5-flash is one of them. Model Access rules decide which models can run.` |

| Rule | The message starts with |
|------|-------------------------|
| A personal account's `account` rule | `Your account` |
| A team's `account` rule | `This team` |
| `member` | `You`, with `in this team` after the model or category, for example `You can't use openai/gpt-6-2-astra in this team.` |
| `project` | `This API key` |
| `surface` | The surface's name: `The dashboard`, `The API`, `MCP`, `The LLM gateway`, `The browser extensions`, `Agents`, `Studio`, `The Workflow Agent` or `Workflows`, for example `Studio can't use openai/gpt-6-2-astra.` |
| `agent` | `This agent` |

Nothing runs and nothing is charged. Retrying does not help: run a model the rules allow, or ask someone who manages the rule to change it. Through the [LLM gateway](/docs/completions-api#gateway-errors) the refusal is an HTTP `403` error with code `model_not_allowed`, and the [MCP server](/docs/wiro-mcp-server) returns it as a tool error.

### Who Can Change Rules

- **Personal account**: its owner
- **Team**: a team admin or the organization owner. The person who created the team is one of its admins

Every team member can read the team's rules with `/ModelAccess/List` and `/ModelAccess/Check`. A member who is not an admin can't change any rule: not their own member rule, and not the rules of the API keys they created or the agents they deployed. A deployed agent's own calls to the `/ModelAccess` endpoints are refused with HTTP `403`, reads included.

### Changing Rules With the API

`/ModelAccess/Set`, `/ModelAccess/Remove` and `/ModelAccess/Preview` work in the dashboard, with a signed-in user's Bearer token and with an API key:

- **With an API key**, the call acts as the person who created the key's project, in that project's workspace: the creator's personal account for a personal project, the team for a team project. The key follows its creator's current role: while the creator is a team member who is not an admin, the key can read rules but not change them.
- **With a Bearer token**, the call acts as you, in your personal account. To work in a team, send the team's guid in the `x-team-guid` header. A call whose `x-team-guid` names a team you are not a member of, and whose organization you don't own, is refused with `You are not a member of this team.` Calls with an API key ignore this header.

`/ModelAccess/List` and `/ModelAccess/Preview` return the `workspace` they work in, so you can check where a change lands before you make it. Changes made with API keys are limited to 60 per workspace in any hour, counting spend limits and Model Access rules together. Preview does not count. Each change is recorded with who made it and how.

## **POST** /ModelAccess/List

Returns the Model Access rules of the call's workspace, the categories a rule can name, and how the call itself counts. A team project's API key reads its team, a personal project's key your personal account, and the dashboard the workspace you have selected (see [Changing Rules With the API](#changing-rules-with-the-api)). Any team member can call it, and it works with an API key. Send an empty body: `{}`.

```json
// Response
{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "workspace": {
    "type": "team",
    "teamguid": "0d9aade4-d31b-4b97-88f3-a90482f080ea",
    "canmanage": false
  },
  "caller": {
    "surface": "api",
    "projectid": "48211"
  },
  "rules": [
    {
      "guid": "a642eda4-68ef-4fa9-af15-7024f28b0332",
      "scope": "account",
      "target": "",
      "targetlabel": null,
      "access": "allow",
      "categories": [
        { "category": "video", "label": "Video Generation", "access": "block" }
      ],
      "models": [
        { "id": "2062", "model": "bytedance/seedance-v2-5-flash", "title": "Seedance v2.5 Flash Video Generator", "access": "allow" }
      ],
      "createdat": 1795180800,
      "updatedat": 1795180800,
      "updatedby": { "useruuid": "c1d2e3f4-a5b6-4c7d-8e9f-0a1b2c3d4e5f", "label": "the organization owner" }
    },
    {
      "guid": "a4308936-5441-4012-96ee-f2b32ad3fd40",
      "scope": "project",
      "target": "48211",
      "targetlabel": "Production",
      "access": "block",
      "categories": [
        { "category": "image", "label": "Image Generation", "access": "allow" }
      ],
      "models": [],
      "createdat": 1795184400,
      "updatedat": 1795188000,
      "updatedby": { "useruuid": "7a1b2c3d-4e5f-4a6b-8c7d-9e0f1a2b3c4d", "label": "John Doe" }
    },
    {
      "guid": "9f12fb7e-16f0-4208-83b6-c333b83192d7",
      "scope": "surface",
      "target": "mcp",
      "targetlabel": "MCP",
      "access": "allow",
      "categories": [
        { "category": "video", "label": "Video Generation", "access": "block" }
      ],
      "models": [],
      "createdat": 1795191600,
      "updatedat": 1795191600,
      "updatedby": { "useruuid": "7a1b2c3d-4e5f-4a6b-8c7d-9e0f1a2b3c4d", "label": "John Doe" }
    }
  ],
  "categories": [
    { "category": "image", "label": "Image Generation", "values": ["text-to-image", "image-to-image", "image-editing", "image-to-text"] },
    { "category": "video", "label": "Video Generation", "values": ["text-to-video", "image-to-video", "video-to-video", "speech-to-video", "talking-head", "video-to-text", "reference-to-video", "audio-to-video", "lip-sync"] },
    { "category": "audio", "label": "Audio & Speech", "values": ["text-to-speech", "speech-to-text", "speech-to-speech", "video-to-music", "voice-clone", "text-to-audio", "image-to-audio", "realtime-conversation", "realtime-tts", "realtime-stt"] },
    { "category": "music", "label": "Music Generation", "values": ["music-generation", "text-to-song", "text-to-music", "image-to-song", "image-to-music"] },
    { "category": "3d", "label": "3D Generation", "values": ["3d-generation", "text-to-3d", "image-to-3d"] },
    { "category": "llm", "label": "LLM & Chat", "values": ["chat", "llm", "partner-llm", "rag", "llm-reasoning"] },
    { "category": "utilities", "label": "Utilities", "values": ["utils"] }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `workspace.type` | `team` or `personal` |
| `workspace.teamguid` | The team's guid, or `null` for a personal account |
| `workspace.canmanage` | Whether the caller can change rules in this workspace: `true` for a personal account's owner, a team admin and the organization owner, also with the API key of a project they created; `false` for other team members and their keys |
| `caller.surface` | The surface this call counts on, such as `api` for a call with an API key (see [Surfaces](#how-model-access-works)) |
| `caller.projectid` | The project id of the API key the call used, or `null` without a key |
| `rules[].guid` | The rule's guid, for `/ModelAccess/Remove` |
| `rules[].scope` | `account`, `member`, `project`, `surface` or `agent` |
| `rules[].target` | The member's `useruuid`, the project id, the surface or the agent's guid; `""` for `account` |
| `rules[].targetlabel` | The member's name, the project's name, the agent's title or the surface's label; `null` for `account` |
| `rules[].access` | Everything Else: `allow` or `block` |
| `rules[].categories` | The categories the rule names, each with its `label` and `access`, in the order of `categories` below |
| `rules[].models` | The models the rule names, in `id` order: `id` (a string), `model` (`owner/slug`), `title` and `access`. `model` and `title` are `null` for a model that is no longer on Wiro |
| `rules[].createdat`, `rules[].updatedat` | When the rule was added and last changed, in Unix seconds |
| `rules[].updatedby` | Who changed the rule last: `useruuid` and `label`, the person's name, or their email when they have no name. In a team, the owner of its organization who is not a member of the team is labeled `the organization owner`, and someone who has left the team has a `null` label. A change made with an API key names the person who created the key's project. `updatedby` is `null` when Wiro changed the rule last, as for the team allowlists and blocklists moved into this system |
| `categories` | The seven categories a rule can name: `category` (the key a rule uses), `label` and `values` (the catalog categories it covers) |

## **POST** /ModelAccess/Set

Adds a rule to the call's workspace, or replaces the rule with the same `scope` and `target`. The rule you send replaces the old one as a whole, so a category or model you leave out is no longer named. Only the people who can change rules can call it (see [Who Can Change Rules](#who-can-change-rules)), in the dashboard, with a Bearer token or with an API key. To check a change first, send the same body to [`/ModelAccess/Preview`](#model-access-preview).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `scope` | string | Yes | `"account"`, `"member"`, `"project"`, `"surface"` or `"agent"`. See [What a Rule Covers](#how-model-access-works) |
| `target` | string | For every scope but `account` | The member's `useruuid`, the project's `id`, the surface (`web`, `api`, `mcp`, `llm-gateway`, `extension`, `agent`, `studio`, `workflow-agent` or `workflow`) or the agent's guid. Leave it out for `account` |
| `access` | string | No | Everything Else: `"allow"` or `"block"`. Default: `"allow"` |
| `categories` | array or object | No | The categories the rule allows or blocks, as `[{ "category": "video", "access": "block" }]` or as `{ "video": "block" }`. A category is `image`, `video`, `audio`, `music`, `3d`, `llm` or `utilities` |
| `models` | array or object | No | The single models the rule allows or blocks, as `[{ "model": "openai/gpt-6-2-astra", "access": "block" }]` or as `{ "openai/gpt-6-2-astra": "block" }`. Name a model by its `owner/slug` or its `id`. At most 500 models |

### Examples

**Block video models for the whole account, except one:**

```json
{
  "scope": "account",
  "access": "allow",
  "categories": [
    { "category": "video", "access": "block" }
  ],
  "models": [
    { "model": "bytedance/seedance-v2-5-flash", "access": "allow" }
  ]
}
```

**Let one API key run only image models:**

```json
{
  "scope": "project",
  "target": "48211",
  "access": "block",
  "categories": [
    { "category": "image", "access": "allow" }
  ]
}
```

**Keep video models out of MCP:**

```json
{
  "scope": "surface",
  "target": "mcp",
  "categories": { "video": "block" }
}
```

**Block one model for one agent:**

```json
{
  "scope": "agent",
  "target": "6e4bbd6f-6b73-4421-adae-e9599ba2e317",
  "models": { "openai/gpt-6-2-astra": "block" }
}
```

`rule` is the rule as saved, shaped like a row of `/ModelAccess/List`:

```json
// Response
{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "rule": {
    "guid": "a4308936-5441-4012-96ee-f2b32ad3fd40",
    "scope": "project",
    "target": "48211",
    "targetlabel": "Production",
    "access": "block",
    "categories": [
      { "category": "image", "label": "Image Generation", "access": "allow" }
    ],
    "models": [],
    "createdat": 1795184400,
    "updatedat": 1795188000,
    "updatedby": { "useruuid": "7a1b2c3d-4e5f-4a6b-8c7d-9e0f1a2b3c4d", "label": "John Doe" }
  }
}
```

### Errors

| Error | Cause |
|-------|-------|
| `scope must be one of account, member, project, surface, agent.` | `scope` is missing or not one of the five scopes |
| `Member rules exist only in a team workspace.` | A `member` rule in a personal account |
| `target is required for this scope.` | No `target` for a `member`, `project`, `surface` or `agent` rule |
| `A surface is one of web, api, mcp, llm-gateway, extension, agent, studio, workflow-agent, workflow.` | A `surface` rule with another `target` |
| `target must be a project id.` | A `project` rule whose `target` is not a project id |
| `access must be allow or block.` | Another `access` |
| `categories must be a list of { category, access }.` | `categories` is neither a list nor an object |
| `A category is one of image, video, audio, music, 3d, llm, utilities.` | A category that is not one of the seven |
| `A category's access must be allow or block.` | A category with another `access` |
| `models must be a list of { model, access }.` | `models` is neither a list nor an object |
| `A rule can name at most 500 models.` | More than 500 models |
| `Each model needs its owner/slug or id.` | A model entry with no model |
| `A model's access must be allow or block.` | A model with another `access` |
| `<model> is not a model's owner/slug or id.` | A model named neither by `owner/slug` nor by a number |
| `<model> is not a model on Wiro.` | No model listed on Wiro has that `owner/slug` or id |
| `<model> is named twice.` | `models` names a model twice: by the same name, or by its id and its `owner/slug` with a different `access` |
| `You are not a member of this team.` | With a Bearer token, `x-team-guid` names a team you are not a member of, and whose organization you don't own |
| `Only a team admin or the organization owner can change this rule.` | In a team, a signed-in caller is not a team admin or the organization owner |
| `This API key acts as the person who created it, who is a member of this team. Only a team admin or the organization owner can change this rule.` | With an API key, the person who created the key's project is a team member who is not an admin |
| `That person is not an active member of this team.` | A `member` rule for someone who is not an active member of the team |
| `That API key's project is not in this workspace.` | A `project` rule for a project of another workspace |
| `That agent is not in this workspace.` | An `agent` rule for an agent of another workspace |
| `Too many changes to Spend Limits and Model Access in the last hour. Try again later.` | With API keys, this workspace's spend limits and Model Access rules have been changed 60 times in the last hour |

## **POST** /ModelAccess/Preview

Shows what `/ModelAccess/Set` would do, and changes nothing. It takes the same body as `/ModelAccess/Set` and checks it the same way, so only the people who can change rules can call it. Use it to see which workspace a change lands in, the rule as it would be saved and the rule it would replace. For an `agent` rule, it also says whether the rule would block the chat model the agent answers with.

### Example

**Let the Support Agent run only image models:**

```json
{
  "scope": "agent",
  "target": "6e4bbd6f-6b73-4421-adae-e9599ba2e317",
  "access": "block",
  "categories": [
    { "category": "image", "access": "allow" }
  ]
}
```

```json
// Response
{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "preview": true,
  "workspace": {
    "type": "team",
    "teamguid": "0d9aade4-d31b-4b97-88f3-a90482f080ea",
    "canmanage": true
  },
  "rule": {
    "guid": "c2f0a9d4-5b7e-4c1a-8e36-9d4b2a7f1e05",
    "scope": "agent",
    "target": "6e4bbd6f-6b73-4421-adae-e9599ba2e317",
    "targetlabel": "Support Agent",
    "access": "block",
    "categories": [
      { "category": "image", "label": "Image Generation", "access": "allow" }
    ],
    "models": [],
    "createdat": 1795195200,
    "updatedat": null,
    "updatedby": null
  },
  "existing": {
    "guid": "c2f0a9d4-5b7e-4c1a-8e36-9d4b2a7f1e05",
    "scope": "agent",
    "target": "6e4bbd6f-6b73-4421-adae-e9599ba2e317",
    "targetlabel": "Support Agent",
    "access": "allow",
    "categories": [
      { "category": "video", "label": "Video Generation", "access": "block" }
    ],
    "models": [],
    "createdat": 1795195200,
    "updatedat": 1795195200,
    "updatedby": { "useruuid": "7a1b2c3d-4e5f-4a6b-8c7d-9e0f1a2b3c4d", "label": "John Doe" }
  },
  "agentchatmodel": {
    "ref": "openai/gpt-5.6-sol",
    "model": "openai/gpt-5-6-sol",
    "blocked": true
  }
}
```

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `preview` | Always `true`: nothing was changed |
| `workspace` | The workspace the change would be made in, as in `/ModelAccess/List`: `type`, `teamguid` and `canmanage`, which is always `true` here |
| `rule` | The rule as `/ModelAccess/Set` would save it, shaped like a row of `/ModelAccess/List`. Its `guid` and `createdat` are those of the rule it would replace, or `null` for a new rule, and its `updatedat` and `updatedby` are `null` |
| `existing` | The current rule with the same `scope` and `target`, which the change would replace, or `null` when there is none |
| `agentchatmodel` | For an `agent` rule only: the chat model the agent answers with, as its settings name it (`ref`) and by its `owner/slug` on Wiro (`model`), and whether the rule would block it (`blocked`) |

When `agentchatmodel.blocked` is `true`, the agent stops answering within about a minute of the rule being saved: its turns end with `[MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED]`. Allow its chat model in the rule too, or allow LLM & Chat. The errors are those of `/ModelAccess/Set`, except that Preview does not count toward the hourly cap on changes made with API keys.

## **POST** /ModelAccess/Remove

Removes a rule from the call's workspace. The people who can change rules can remove one, in the dashboard, with a Bearer token or with an API key.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `guid` | string | Yes | The rule's `guid` from `/ModelAccess/List` |

```json
// Response
{
  "result": true,
  "errors": []
}
```

| Error | Cause |
|-------|-------|
| `guid is required.` | No `guid` was sent |
| `Rule not found in this workspace.` | The guid is not a rule of the call's workspace, or it was already removed |
| `You are not a member of this team.` | With a Bearer token, `x-team-guid` names a team you are not a member of, and whose organization you don't own |
| `Only a team admin or the organization owner can change this rule.` | In a team, a signed-in caller is not a team admin or the organization owner |
| `This API key acts as the person who created it, who is a member of this team. Only a team admin or the organization owner can change this rule.` | With an API key, the person who created the key's project is a team member who is not an admin |
| `Too many changes to Spend Limits and Model Access in the last hour. Try again later.` | With API keys, this workspace's spend limits and Model Access rules have been changed 60 times in the last hour |

## **POST** /ModelAccess/Check

Shows how the rules of the call's workspace decide one model for one run: which rules apply, what each one decides and why, and the refusal the run would get. Nothing runs. A team project's API key reads its team, a personal project's key your personal account, and the dashboard the workspace you have selected. Any team member can call it, and it works with an API key. With only `model`, it checks a dashboard run of yours. To check another run, name it with `member`, `project`, `agent` or `surface`. `check.context` in the response says which run was checked.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `model` | string | Yes | The model's `owner/slug` or `id` |
| `member` | string | No | In a team, the `useruuid` of the member whose dashboard run to check. Default: you (with an API key, the person who created its project). With `project` or `agent`, the run is checked as the person who created that API key, and `member` is not used |
| `project` | string | No | A project's `id`, to check a run made with that project's API key, as the person who created the project. The surface is then `api` unless you name another one, and `web` is refused: a run made with an API key never counts as the dashboard |
| `surface` | string | No | Where the run comes from: `web`, `api`, `mcp`, `llm-gateway`, `extension`, `agent`, `studio`, `workflow-agent` or `workflow`. Default: `web`, a dashboard run. With `project` the default is `api`, and with `agent` the surface is always `agent`. The `agent` surface needs an agent: send its guid in `agent` |
| `agent` | string | No | An agent's guid, to check a model run that agent makes: with the API key it runs models with, as the person who created that key, on the `agent` surface. `project` is not used then |

### Example

**Can the Production API key run `openai/gpt-6-2-astra`?**

```json
{
  "model": "openai/gpt-6-2-astra",
  "project": "48211",
  "surface": "api"
}
```

Each applicable rule comes back shaped like a row of `/ModelAccess/List`, with what it decides. This workspace is a team, so `check.context` shows the key's run checked as Jane Doe, who created the Production project:

```json
// Response
{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "check": {
    "model": "openai/gpt-6-2-astra",
    "categories": ["llm"],
    "allowed": false,
    "message": "This API key can only use selected models, and openai/gpt-6-2-astra is not one of them. Model Access rules decide which models can run.",
    "rules": [
      {
        "rule": {
          "guid": "a642eda4-68ef-4fa9-af15-7024f28b0332",
          "scope": "account",
          "target": "",
          "targetlabel": null,
          "access": "allow",
          "categories": [
            { "category": "video", "label": "Video Generation", "access": "block" }
          ],
          "models": [
            { "id": "2062", "model": "bytedance/seedance-v2-5-flash", "title": "Seedance v2.5 Flash Video Generator", "access": "allow" }
          ],
          "createdat": 1795180800,
          "updatedat": 1795180800,
          "updatedby": { "useruuid": "c1d2e3f4-a5b6-4c7d-8e9f-0a1b2c3d4e5f", "label": "the organization owner" }
        },
        "access": "allow",
        "by": "default",
        "category": null
      },
      {
        "rule": {
          "guid": "a4308936-5441-4012-96ee-f2b32ad3fd40",
          "scope": "project",
          "target": "48211",
          "targetlabel": "Production",
          "access": "block",
          "categories": [
            { "category": "image", "label": "Image Generation", "access": "allow" }
          ],
          "models": [],
          "createdat": 1795184400,
          "updatedat": 1795188000,
          "updatedby": { "useruuid": "7a1b2c3d-4e5f-4a6b-8c7d-9e0f1a2b3c4d", "label": "John Doe" }
        },
        "access": "block",
        "by": "default",
        "category": null
      }
    ],
    "context": {
      "surface": "api",
      "member": { "useruuid": "3f5a9c20-6d41-4b8e-a1c7-5e9d0f2b4c61", "label": "Jane Doe" },
      "project": { "projectid": "48211", "label": "Production" },
      "agent": null
    }
  }
}
```

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `check.model` | The model as `owner/slug` |
| `check.categories` | The categories the model is in, such as `["llm"]`. Empty when it is in none |
| `check.allowed` | Whether every rule that applies allows the model |
| `check.message` | The refusal a run would get with code `92`, or `null` when the model is allowed |
| `check.rules` | The rules that apply, in the order account, member, API key, surface, agent. Empty when none applies |
| `check.rules[].rule` | The rule, shaped like a row of `/ModelAccess/List` |
| `check.rules[].access` | What this rule decides: `allow` or `block` |
| `check.rules[].by` | What decided it: `model` (the model's own entry), `category` (one of its categories) or `default` (Everything Else) |
| `check.rules[].category` | The category that decided it when `by` is `category`, else `null` |
| `check.context` | Which run was checked: `surface`, `member`, `project` and `agent` |
| `check.context.surface` | The surface the run was checked on: the `surface` you sent, else `api` with `project` and `web` without it. Always `agent` with `agent` |
| `check.context.member` | In a team, the member the run was checked as: `useruuid`, and the member's name as `label`. That is the `member` you sent, else you, and with `project` or `agent` the person who created that API key. `null` in a personal account |
| `check.context.project` | The project whose API key the run was checked with: `projectid`, and the project's name as `label`. That is the `project` you sent, or for an agent the Wiro project it runs models with. `null` without `project` or `agent` |
| `check.context.agent` | The agent whose run was checked: `useragentguid`, and the agent's title as `label`. `null` without `agent` |

| Error | Cause |
|-------|-------|
| `model is required.` | No `model` was sent |
| `<model> is not a model's owner/slug or id.` | `model` is neither an `owner/slug` nor a number |
| `<model> is not a model on Wiro.` | No model listed on Wiro has that `owner/slug` or id |
| `A surface is one of web, api, mcp, llm-gateway, extension, agent, studio, workflow-agent, workflow.` | Another `surface` |
| `Name the agent to check its runs.` | `surface` is `agent` and no `agent` was sent |
| `That API key's project is not in this workspace.` | `project` is not the id of a project of this workspace |
| `A run made with an API key never counts as the dashboard. Leave surface out or pick another one.` | `project` with `surface` `web` |
| `That agent is not in this workspace.` | `agent` is not the guid of an agent of this workspace |
| `That agent has no API key to run models with yet.` | The agent has no Wiro project to run models with yet: connect one with [`/UserAgent/CredentialProjectBind`](/docs/agent-overview#post-useragentcredentialprojectbind) |
| `That agent runs models with an API key of another workspace, so that workspace's rules decide them.` | The Wiro project the agent runs models with is in another workspace |

# Error Reference

Understand API error responses, error codes, and how to handle them.

## Error Codes

| Code | Category | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| `0` | General | Server-side errors, validation failures, missing parameters |
| `1` | Not Found | Resource not found or not accessible |
| `92` | Model Access | A Model Access rule of the workspace blocks the model. See [Model Access](/docs/model-access) |
| `93` | Spend Limit | A spend limit of the workspace is reached. See [Spend Limits](/docs/spend-limits) |
| `96` | Concurrency Limit | Too many concurrent tasks for your balance |
| `97` | Insufficient Balance | Not enough funds to run the model |
| `98` | Authentication Required | Sign in required to access this model |
| `99` | Token Invalid | Bearer token missing, invalid, or expired |

## Error Response Format

```json
{
  "result": false,
  "errors": [{ "code": 97, "message": "Insufficient balance" }]
}
```

All API responses return HTTP `200`. Auth errors return HTTP `401`.

## Team API Key Errors

| Code | Message | When |
|------|---------|------|
| `0` | The person who created this API key is no longer in its team. Ask a team admin for a new key. | HTTP `401`: the user who created the team project left the team |
| `0` | API keys can't manage teams or organizations. Sign in and try again. | HTTP `401`: an organization, team, member or transfer change sent with an API key |
| `0` | You must be a member of this team to perform this action | HTTP `403`: a Studio or Workflow Agent request with a team key whose creator is the organization owner but not a member of the team |

Public endpoints such as `Tool/List` and `Agent/List` still answer a key whose creator left the team, as if the request had no key.

## Run Errors (POST /Run)

| Code | Message | Action |
|------|---------|--------|
| `92` | Model blocked by a Model Access rule (the message names the rule) | Run a model the rules allow, or ask someone who manages the rule to change it under [Controls > Model Access](https://wiro.ai/panel/controls/model-access); retrying does not help before that |
| `93` | Spend limit reached (the message names the limit and when it resets) | Wait for the reset, or have someone who manages the limit raise it under [Controls > Spend Limits](https://wiro.ai/panel/controls/spend-limits); retrying does not help before that |
| `96` | Concurrent task limit reached | Wait for task to finish or add funds |
| `97` | Insufficient balance | Add funds ($0.50 min, $10 for training) |
| `98` | Sign in required | Model requires registered account |
| `0` | Parameter required/invalid | Fix request parameters |
| `1` | Model not found/accessible | Check model slug |

## Task Errors (POST /Task)

| Code | Message | Endpoint |
|------|---------|----------|
| `0` | Task not found | Detail, Kill, InputOutputDelete |
| `1` | Task not found | Cancel |
| `1` | Not cancellable | Cancel |
| `1` | Kill failed | Kill |
| `0` | Task not completed | InputOutputDelete |
| `0` | Missing identifier | Detail, Kill |
| `0` | Permission denied | Detail, Cancel |

# Code Examples

Complete end-to-end examples in all 9 supported languages.

## Overview

Each example below demonstrates the full Wiro workflow: authenticate, run a model, poll for task completion, and retrieve the result. Choose your preferred language.

- **curl**: Shell scripting with bash
- **Python**: Using the `requests` library
- **Node.js**: Using `axios`
- **PHP**: Using cURL functions
- **C#**: Using `HttpClient` (.NET 6+)
- **Swift**: Using async/await `URLSession`
- **Dart**: Using the `http` package
- **Kotlin**: Using `java.net.http`
- **Go**: Using the standard library `net/http`

## Full Examples

All examples perform the same steps:

1. Set up authentication headers
2. Run a model (`POST /Run/{owner-slug}/{model-slug}`)
3. Poll the task status (`POST /Task/Detail`)
4. Print the final output

### curl

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Wiro API — End-to-End Example (curl)

API_KEY="YOUR_API_KEY"
BASE_URL="https://api.wiro.ai/v1"

# 1. Run a model
echo "Starting model run..."
RUN_RESPONSE=$(curl -s -X POST "$BASE_URL/Run/{owner-slug}/{model-slug}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-api-key: $API_KEY" \
  -d '{"prompt": "A cyberpunk cityscape at night", "width": 1024, "height": 1024}')

TASK_ID=$(echo "$RUN_RESPONSE" | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['taskid'])")
TASK_TOKEN=$(echo "$RUN_RESPONSE" | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['socketaccesstoken'])")
echo "Task ID: $TASK_ID"

# 2. Poll for results
while true; do
  TASK_RESPONSE=$(curl -s -X POST "$BASE_URL/Task/Detail" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -H "x-api-key: $API_KEY" \
    -d "{\"tasktoken\": \"$TASK_TOKEN\"}")

  STATUS=$(echo "$TASK_RESPONSE" | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['tasklist'][0]['status'])")
  echo "Status: $STATUS"

  if [ "$STATUS" = "task_postprocess_end" ]; then
    echo "Done! Output:"
    echo $TASK_RESPONSE | python3 -m json.tool
    break
  elif [ "$STATUS" = "task_cancel" ]; then
    echo "Task cancelled"
    break
  fi

  sleep 3
done
```

### Python

```python
import requests
import time

API_KEY = "YOUR_API_KEY"
BASE_URL = "https://api.wiro.ai/v1"

headers = {
    "x-api-key": API_KEY,
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
}

# 1. Run a model
print("Starting model run...")
run_resp = requests.post(
    f"{BASE_URL}/Run/{owner-slug}/{model-slug}",
    headers=headers,
    json={
        "prompt": "A cyberpunk cityscape at night",
        "width": 1024,
        "height": 1024
    }
)
run_data = run_resp.json()
task_token = run_data["socketaccesstoken"]
print(f"Task ID: {run_data['taskid']}")

# 2. Poll for results
while True:
    task_resp = requests.post(
        f"{BASE_URL}/Task/Detail",
        headers=headers,
        json={"tasktoken": task_token}
    )
    task = task_resp.json()["tasklist"][0]
    status = task["status"]
    print(f"Status: {status}")

    if status == "task_postprocess_end":
        print("Done! Outputs:", task.get("outputs"))
        break
    elif status == "task_cancel":
        print("Task cancelled")
        break

    time.sleep(3)
```

### Node.js

```javascript
const axios = require('axios');

const API_KEY = 'YOUR_API_KEY';
const BASE_URL = 'https://api.wiro.ai/v1';

const headers = {
  'x-api-key': API_KEY,
  'Content-Type': 'application/json'
};

async function main() {
  // 1. Run a model
  console.log('Starting model run...');
  const runResp = await axios.post(
    `${BASE_URL}/Run/{owner-slug}/{model-slug}`,
    {
      prompt: 'A cyberpunk cityscape at night',
      width: 1024,
      height: 1024
    },
    { headers }
  );
  const taskToken = runResp.data.socketaccesstoken;
  console.log('Task ID:', runResp.data.taskid);

  // 2. Poll for results
  while (true) {
    const taskResp = await axios.post(
      `${BASE_URL}/Task/Detail`,
      { tasktoken: taskToken },
      { headers }
    );
    const task = taskResp.data.tasklist[0];
    const { status } = task;
    console.log('Status:', status);

    if (status === 'task_postprocess_end') {
      console.log('Done! Outputs:', task.outputs);
      break;
    }
    if (status === 'task_cancel') {
      console.log('Task cancelled');
      break;
    }

    await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 3000));
  }
}

main();
```

### PHP

```php
<?php
$apiKey = 'YOUR_API_KEY';
$baseUrl = 'https://api.wiro.ai/v1';

function apiPost($url, $data, $apiKey) {
    $ch = curl_init($url);
    curl_setopt_array($ch, [
        CURLOPT_POST => true,
        CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true,
        CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER => [
            'Content-Type: application/json',
            'x-api-key: ' . $apiKey,
        ],
        CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS => json_encode($data),
    ]);
    $response = curl_exec($ch);
    curl_close($ch);
    return json_decode($response, true);
}

// 1. Run a model
echo "Starting model run...\n";
$runResp = apiPost("$baseUrl/Run/{owner-slug}/{model-slug}", [
    'prompt' => 'A cyberpunk cityscape at night',
    'width' => 1024,
    'height' => 1024,
], $apiKey);
$taskToken = $runResp['socketaccesstoken'];
echo "Task ID: {$runResp['taskid']}\n";

// 2. Poll for results
while (true) {
    $taskResp = apiPost("$baseUrl/Task/Detail", [
        'tasktoken' => $taskToken,
    ], $apiKey);
    $task = $taskResp['tasklist'][0];
    $status = $task['status'];
    echo "Status: $status\n";

    if ($status === 'task_postprocess_end') {
        echo "Done! Outputs:\n";
        print_r($task['outputs']);
        break;
    }
    if ($status === 'task_cancel') {
        echo "Task cancelled\n";
        break;
    }

    sleep(3);
}
```

### Swift

```swift
import Foundation

let apiKey = "YOUR_API_KEY"
let baseUrl = "https://api.wiro.ai/v1"

func apiPost(_ endpoint: String, body: [String: Any]) async throws -> [String: Any] {
    var request = URLRequest(url: URL(string: "\(baseUrl)\(endpoint)")!)
    request.httpMethod = "POST"
    request.addValue("application/json", forHTTPHeaderField: "Content-Type")
    request.addValue(apiKey, forHTTPHeaderField: "x-api-key")
    request.httpBody = try JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: body)

    let (data, _) = try await URLSession.shared.data(for: request)
    return try JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: data) as! [String: Any]
}

// 1. Run a model
print("Starting model run...")
let runResp = try await apiPost("/Run/{owner-slug}/{model-slug}", body: [
    "prompt": "A cyberpunk cityscape at night",
    "width": 1024,
    "height": 1024
])
let taskToken = runResp["socketaccesstoken"] as! String
print("Task ID: \(runResp["taskid"] ?? "")")

// 2. Poll for results
while true {
    let taskResp = try await apiPost("/Task/Detail", body: ["tasktoken": taskToken])
    let taskData = (taskResp["tasklist"] as! [[String: Any]])[0]
    let status = taskData["status"] as! String
    print("Status: \(status)")

    if status == "task_postprocess_end" {
        print("Done! Outputs: \(taskData["outputs"] ?? [])")
        break
    }
    if status == "task_cancel" {
        print("Task cancelled")
        break
    }

    try await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 3_000_000_000)
}
```

### Kotlin

```kotlin
import java.net.URI
import java.net.http.HttpClient
import java.net.http.HttpRequest
import java.net.http.HttpResponse
import com.google.gson.Gson
import com.google.gson.JsonObject

val apiKey = "YOUR_API_KEY"
val baseUrl = "https://api.wiro.ai/v1"
val client = HttpClient.newHttpClient()
val gson = Gson()

fun apiPost(endpoint: String, body: Map<String, Any?>): JsonObject {
    val request = HttpRequest.newBuilder()
        .uri(URI.create("$baseUrl$endpoint"))
        .header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        .header("x-api-key", apiKey)
        .POST(HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.ofString(gson.toJson(body)))
        .build()
    val response = client.send(request, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString())
    return gson.fromJson(response.body(), JsonObject::class.java)
}

fun main() {
    // 1. Run a model
    println("Starting model run...")
    val runResp = apiPost("/Run/{owner-slug}/{model-slug}", mapOf(
        "prompt" to "A cyberpunk cityscape at night",
        "width" to 1024,
        "height" to 1024
    ))
    val taskToken = runResp.get("socketaccesstoken").asString
    println("Task ID: ${runResp.get("taskid").asString}")

    // 2. Poll for results
    while (true) {
        val taskResp = apiPost("/Task/Detail", mapOf("tasktoken" to taskToken))
        val taskData = taskResp.getAsJsonArray("tasklist")[0].asJsonObject
        val status = taskData.get("status").asString
        println("Status: $status")

        when (status) {
            "task_postprocess_end" -> {
                println("Done! Outputs: ${taskData.get("outputs")}")
                return
            }
            "task_cancel" -> {
                println("Task cancelled")
                return
            }
        }

        Thread.sleep(3000)
    }
}
```

### Go

```go
package main

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"time"
)

const (
	apiKey  = "YOUR_API_KEY"
	baseURL = "https://api.wiro.ai/v1"
)

func apiPost(endpoint string, body map[string]interface{}) (map[string]interface{}, error) {
	jsonBody, _ := json.Marshal(body)
	req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", baseURL+endpoint, bytes.NewBuffer(jsonBody))
	req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	req.Header.Set("x-api-key", apiKey)

	resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()

	data, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
	var result map[string]interface{}
	json.Unmarshal(data, &result)
	return result, nil
}

func main() {
	// 1. Run a model
	fmt.Println("Starting model run...")
	runResp, _ := apiPost("/Run/{owner-slug}/{model-slug}", map[string]interface{}{
		"prompt": "A cyberpunk cityscape at night",
		"width":  1024,
		"height": 1024,
	})
	taskToken := runResp["socketaccesstoken"].(string)
	fmt.Printf("Task ID: %s\n", runResp["taskid"].(string))

	// 2. Poll for results
	for {
		taskResp, _ := apiPost("/Task/Detail", map[string]interface{}{
			"tasktoken": taskToken,
		})
		taskData := taskResp["tasklist"].([]interface{})[0].(map[string]interface{})
		status := taskData["status"].(string)
		fmt.Printf("Status: %s\n", status)

		switch status {
		case "task_postprocess_end":
			fmt.Printf("Done! Outputs: %v\n", taskData["outputs"])
			return
		case "task_cancel":
			fmt.Println("Task cancelled")
			return
		}

		time.Sleep(3 * time.Second)
	}
}
```
