# MCP Server

Connect AI assistants to Wiro's models, workflows, Studio and agents through the Model Context Protocol.

## Connect with a browser sign-in

**Easiest way.** No API key to copy. Add `https://mcp.wiro.ai/v1` as a remote
MCP server in your app, then sign in with your Wiro account when the app asks.
Works with ChatGPT, Claude, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Gemini CLI, Codex,
Devin, Kiro, goose and Grok.

1. **Add the server.** Add a remote MCP server with the URL `https://mcp.wiro.ai/v1`, without an `Authorization` header.
2. **Sign in to Wiro.** The app opens wiro.ai. Sign in, or create an account.
3. **Pick a project and how long.** Runs are paid from the project's workspace wallet. The app stays connected for 90 days unless you pick another length, from 7 days to unlimited.
4. **Click Allow.** The browser goes back to the app.

One-click install: [Add to Cursor](https://cursor.com/install-mcp?name=wiro&config=eyJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL21jcC53aXJvLmFpL3YxIn0=),
[Install in VS Code](https://vscode.dev/redirect/mcp/install?name=wiro&config=%7B%22type%22%3A%22http%22%2C%22url%22%3A%22https%3A%2F%2Fmcp.wiro.ai%2Fv1%22%7D),
[Add to Kiro](https://kiro.dev/launch/mcp/add/?name=wiro&config=%7B%22url%22%3A%22https%3A%2F%2Fmcp.wiro.ai%2Fv1%22%7D),
[Add to goose](https://goose-docs.ai/extension/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fmcp.wiro.ai%2Fv1&type=streamable_http&id=wiro&name=Wiro%20AI&description=Run%20image%2C%20video%2C%20audio%20and%20LLM%20models%20on%20Wiro%20AI).

Claude, ChatGPT and Devin have no one-click link yet. Open the app's connector
settings and paste the URL above:
[Claude connectors](https://claude.ai/customize/connectors),
[ChatGPT plugins](https://chatgpt.com/plugins),
[Devin MCP settings](https://app.devin.ai/customize?tab=mcps).

## What is MCP?

[Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) (MCP) is an open standard that lets AI assistants use external tools directly. With the Wiro MCP server, your AI assistant can find and run models, build and run workflows, create media with Studio, deploy and talk to your own agents, and check or change your spend limits and Model Access rules, all without leaving your editor or chat app.

The hosted MCP server is available at `mcp.wiro.ai/v1`. Most apps connect with
the browser sign-in above. Clients that send custom request headers, including
Cursor, Claude Code, Windsurf, Kiro, goose, OpenClaw, and Hermes, can use your
API key instead. Claude Desktop can add the hosted URL as a custom connector, or
run Wiro's official local `npx` package.

## Browser sign-in details

ChatGPT, Claude (claude.ai, Claude Desktop and Claude Code), Cursor, VS Code,
Gemini CLI, Codex, Zed, Devin, Kiro, goose, Grok, Grok Bot, Cline and MCP
Inspector connect this way, and so does any app on your computer that follows
the MCP authorization spec. An app that signs in through its own website needs
its callback on Wiro's list; write to support@wiro.ai to add one.

Team members can connect the projects they created; team admins and the
organization owner any project of the team. A project with an IP whitelist only
accepts calls from the addresses on it; ChatGPT and Claude call from their own
servers.

You pick how long an app stays connected on the sign-in page: 7 days, 30 days,
90 days (the default), 180 days, 1 year, or unlimited. Connected apps are
listed under [Projects, Connected Apps](https://wiro.ai/panel/project?view=apps)
with their project, last use and end date; pick a new length there (it counts
from that day), or **Disconnect** to end an app's access within a minute. An
unlimited connection lasts until you disconnect it, and any connection ends when
its project is removed or when you leave the team or lose the role that allowed
it. The same happens once the project's API key stops working, for example when
the person who created a team project leaves the team; the sign-in page then no
longer offers that project. Access tokens last one hour and renew on their own.

For client developers: protected resource metadata at
`https://mcp.wiro.ai/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/v1`, authorization
server metadata at `https://mcp.wiro.ai/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`,
authorization code with PKCE (`S256`), Client ID Metadata Documents or dynamic
client registration at `https://mcp.wiro.ai/register`, resource
`https://mcp.wiro.ai/v1`, scope `mcp`, `iss` on authorization responses.
Sign-in returns only to known apps' callbacks and to loopback addresses (any
port); write to support@wiro.ai to add a callback.

## Setup

### Cursor

Sign in with your browser: click [Add to Cursor](https://cursor.com/install-mcp?name=wiro&config=eyJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL21jcC53aXJvLmFpL3YxIn0=), or add
`{"mcpServers": {"wiro": {"url": "https://mcp.wiro.ai/v1"}}}` to `mcp.json`; Cursor
asks you to sign in to Wiro the first time it connects.

Or use your API key: open MCP settings (`Cmd+Shift+P` → "Open MCP settings") and add:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "wiro": {
      "url": "https://mcp.wiro.ai/v1",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_API_KEY:YOUR_API_SECRET"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Claude Code

#### Sign in with your browser

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http wiro https://mcp.wiro.ai/v1
```

Then run `/mcp` inside Claude Code, pick **wiro** and sign in to Wiro in your
browser.

#### Or install as a plugin

Run these two commands inside Claude Code:

```
/plugin marketplace add wiroai/Wiro-Plugin
/plugin install wiro-ai@wiro
```

Then open `/mcp`, pick the Wiro server and choose **Authenticate** to sign in
to Wiro in your browser. The plugin comes from the
[wiroai/Wiro-Plugin](https://github.com/wiroai/Wiro-Plugin) repository.

The plugin also adds slash commands, such as `/wiro-ai:image`,
`/wiro-ai:video` and `/wiro-ai:speech`, and five agent skills. Each command
picks a model from the catalog, shows the price and waits for your yes before a paid run and can save
the results into your project.

#### Or add the server with your API key

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http wiro \
  https://mcp.wiro.ai/v1 \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY:YOUR_API_SECRET"
```

For API Key Only authentication, use `Bearer YOUR_API_KEY`. Verify with
`claude mcp get wiro` or `/mcp` inside Claude Code.

### Claude Desktop

The quickest way is a custom connector: open
[Connectors](https://claude.ai/customize/connectors) in Claude, click **Add
custom connector**, enter the URL `https://mcp.wiro.ai/v1` and sign in with
your Wiro account when Claude asks. The same connector works on claude.ai.

Or install Node.js 20 or later and add this local stdio entry to
`claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "wiro": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@wiro-ai/wiro-mcp@latest"],
      "env": {
        "WIRO_API_KEY": "YOUR_API_KEY",
        "WIRO_API_SECRET": "YOUR_API_SECRET"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

For API Key Only authentication, remove `WIRO_API_SECRET` completely. Fully quit
and reopen Claude Desktop after saving. The `@latest` in `args`
makes `npx` look up the newest version on npm at every start, so it does not
reuse an older cached build. This runs the local package and provides the same
Wiro tools.

Claude Desktop may enforce a fixed client-side tool timeout. Wiro returns from
each generation wait within 45 seconds; when `nextAction.tool` is
`wait_for_task`, execute that action with the returned arguments until the
existing task completes. Never submit `run_model` again for the same request.
Adding a `timeout` field to `claude_desktop_config.json` is not a reliable
workaround because Claude Desktop versions may ignore it.

### ChatGPT

In ChatGPT, open [Plugins](https://chatgpt.com/plugins), click **+**, choose
**Add custom MCP server**, enter `https://mcp.wiro.ai/v1` and create the
plugin. ChatGPT opens wiro.ai, where you sign in and pick a project. ChatGPT calls Wiro from its
own servers, so pick a project that is open to all IP addresses.

Codex sends the variable as `Authorization: Bearer`, so keep it in your shell

### Kiro

#### Sign in with your browser

[Add to Kiro](https://kiro.dev/launch/mcp/add/?name=wiro&config=%7B%22url%22%3A%22https%3A%2F%2Fmcp.wiro.ai%2Fv1%22%7D),

## Authentication

Signature-Based: `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY:YOUR_API_SECRET`

API Key Only: `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY`

### Authentication errors

A failed tool call comes back as a normal tool result with `isError: true`. Its
text starts with `Wiro API error` and the HTTP status, then a message that says
what to fix. For example, when a project uses signature-based auth and only its
API key was sent:

```json
{
  "isError": true,
  "content": [{
    "type": "text",
    "text": "## Error\n\nWiro API error 401: This project uses signature-based auth. Enter API_KEY:API_SECRET (the key and secret joined with a colon) as the API key."
  }]
}
```

Messages you may see while connecting:

| Message | What to do |
|---------|------------|
| `This project uses signature-based auth. Enter API_KEY:API_SECRET (the key and secret joined with a colon) as the API key.` | Only the API key was sent, but the project uses signature-based auth. Enter `API_KEY:API_SECRET` in the plugin's key field, or send `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY:YOUR_API_SECRET`. |
| `Project authorization is not founded.` | No project has this API key. Copy the key again from your project page. |
| `Project authorization is not valid.` | The API secret does not match the API key. Check that both come from the same project. |
| `Requested ip {ip} is not allowed.` | The project has an IP whitelist, and the address in the message is not on it. Check the whitelist in your project settings. |
| `The person who created this API key is no longer in its team. Ask a team admin for a new key.` | The user who created this team project has left the team, so its key no longer works. Use a key from another project, or sign in again and pick another project. |

A request without an `Authorization` header never reaches a tool. The MCP
endpoint answers HTTP `401` with `Missing or invalid Authorization header` in
the body and a `WWW-Authenticate` header that points apps to the sign-in; an
expired or disconnected sign-in gets the same answer with
`error="invalid_token"`. See [Error Reference](/docs/error-reference) for every
Wiro API error.

## Available Tools

**Model slugs:** Use the clean/lowercase format `owner/model` (e.g. `openai/sora-2`, `wiro/virtual-try-on`). These correspond to the `cleanslugowner/cleanslugproject` values returned by `search_models`.

The server has 56 tools: four groups (Models, Workflows, Agents, Controls) and
three tools that are always available.

| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `search_models` | Search models by keyword, category, or owner |
| `get_model_schema` | Get parameter schema and pricing for any model, or the parameters and output ports of a workflow utility |
| `recommend_model` | Find models for a goal from two or three key words, best matches first |
| `explore` | Browse curated models by category |
| `run_model` | Run any model; waits up to 45 seconds by default, then returns a recoverable task token |
| `wait_for_task` | Continue waiting for an existing task without creating a duplicate run |
| `get_task` | Check task status immediately or wait up to 45 seconds with `wait_seconds` |
| `list_tasks` | Browse authenticated generation history and continue with `get_task` |
| `get_task_price` | Get the cost of a completed task |
| `cancel_task` | Cancel a queued task |
| `kill_task` | Stop a queued or running task |
| `upload_file` | Upload a file from a public http(s) URL for use as model input |

Workflows ([Workflows](/docs/workflows), [Workflow Agent](/docs/workflow-agent)):

| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `list_workflows` | List your workspace's workflows, or search the public gallery by text, tag or model |
| `get_workflow` | Read a workflow's inputs, outputs and step graph |
| `create_workflow` | Save a new workflow from a step graph; every problem comes back at once |
| `update_workflow` | Edit title, description, tags or graph without overwriting newer changes; a new graph needs your confirmation |
| `clone_workflow` | Copy a public workflow into your workspace |
| `delete_workflow` | Delete a workflow, after your confirmation |
| `run_workflow` | Run a workflow and wait for its outputs; can stop after a chosen step |
| `wait_for_workflow_run` | Keep waiting on a run, read its outputs, or see why a step failed |
| `resume_workflow_run` | Continue a failed or stopped run without paying again for finished steps |
| `list_workflow_runs` | Browse past and current runs, including runs started on wiro.ai |
| `save_workflow_from_agent` | Save a Workflow Agent proposal as a new workflow, or onto an existing one after your confirmation |

Agents ([Studio](/docs/studio), [Agent Overview](/docs/agent-overview)). `agent`
is `"studio"`, `"workflow-agent"` or the guid of one of your own agents:

| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `send_agent_message` | Send a message and wait for the reply, with any media, workflows or model runs it produced |
| `get_agent_message` | Keep waiting on a reply, or read one again |
| `get_agent_conversation` | List conversations, or read one conversation's history |
| `cancel_agent_message` | Stop a reply that is still being written |
| `delete_agent_session` | Delete a conversation and the agent's memory of it, after your confirmation |
| `list_studio_results` | List the images, videos and other results Studio generated for you |
| `list_agent_templates` | Browse ready-made agent templates and the three monthly plans |
| `get_agent_template` | Read a template's skills, plans, the connectors it suggests and the keys it needs |
| `list_agent_connectors` | Browse the connectors an agent can connect (ad accounts, stores, social accounts, mailboxes, data sources), what each one needs and the tools it gives the agent; with an agent, its connections |
| `list_agent_skills` | Browse the skills an agent can have, and what each one needs to work |
| `deploy_agent` | Deploy an agent from a template or build one from skills, on the Starter, Pro or Max plan; shows the plan's price and the AI usage it includes, the Wiro balance that pays it and the other plans' prices, and asks before charging |
| `list_my_agents` | List your agents with their status, plan, AI usage and this month's spending |
| `get_my_agent` | Read one agent's setup, plan, AI usage and the balance it runs on; can wait until it is running |
| `control_agent` | Start, stop or restart an agent |
| `update_agent` | Change an agent's name, description, time zone, models, chat commands and setup from chat |
| `apply_agent_skills` | Turn skills on or off; every plan includes every skill, so a change costs nothing |
| `set_agent_credentials` | Save an agent's chat channel keys (such as a Telegram bot token), Twilio Voice and settings |
| `connect_agent_connector` | Connect a connector to an agent: save its keys, or start its sign-in, which you approve in your browser. A connector that runs with a Wiro project shows the project and its wallet first |
| `set_agent_connector_accounts` | Choose the accounts a connected connector may act on, such as its ad accounts, pages or channels |
| `disconnect_agent_connector` | Disconnect a connector from an agent, after your confirmation |
| `list_projects` | List the projects of the connected project's workspace, to pick one for an agent; no keys are shown |
| `bind_agent_project` | Connect an agent to a Wiro project so it can run models, with no key in the chat; shows the project first, then asks for your confirmation |
| `manage_agent_custom_skill` | Add, edit, schedule, restore or remove an agent's own instructions and scheduled tasks; turning off its approval policy or changing its rules needs your confirmation |
| `manage_agent_billing` | Subscribe, move to another plan, cancel or renew, paid from your Wiro balance, after your confirmation; `buy_credits` is retired and charges nothing |
| `get_agent_activity` | Read an agent's AI usage, its transactions in dollars and its activity logs, including who changed what on it |
| `delete_agent` | Delete an agent, after your confirmation |

**Setup changes from chat.** A reply from one of your agents can propose a
change to its own setup, such as connecting a connector, adding a skill, or
creating a scheduled task (see
[Setup From Chat](/docs/agent-messaging#setup-from-chat)). The assistant shows
you the proposal and never approves it on its own. When you agree, it sends
your yes as the next message: Wiro answers the first yes with the exact
change, and your next yes (or `yes 2` for the second of several changes)
applies it. Keys never go in a chat message: the assistant connects a
connector with `connect_agent_connector`, and saves a channel's key with
`set_agent_credentials`. This works while the
agent's setup from chat is `all`, the default, which `deploy_agent` and
`update_agent` set with `chat_setup`. With `webchat`, apply the change in the
agent's chat on wiro.ai; with `off`, the agent asks for it on the agent page.

Session names use letters, digits, dots, dashes, underscores and colons, up to
128 characters (100 for the Workflow Agent), and can't end in `-r` followed by
a number. Studio refuses a message under any other name; a Studio session that
already has another name can still be read and deleted.

Controls ([Spend Limits](/docs/spend-limits), [Model Access](/docs/model-access)). Only a personal
account's owner, a team admin or the organization owner can change limits and
rules, and a connection acts as the person who created its project:

| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `get_controls` | Read the workspace's spend limits, with what each has used and when it resets, its Model Access rules, and whether this connection can change them; on request, also this month's or today's spending by surface, member, API key and agent |
| `check_model_access` | Explain whether a model may run here and why, rule by rule. Nothing runs and nothing is charged |
| `manage_spend_limit` | Set or remove a spend limit, after your confirmation |
| `manage_model_access` | Update, replace or remove a Model Access rule, after your confirmation |

The two manage tools show a change summary first and change nothing until you
confirm.

Always available:

| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `get_account` | Show which workspace the connected project belongs to, its wallet balance, its spend limits (each with what it has used this period and whether it is used up) and, when you ask (`recent_transactions`, `transactions_start`), the wallet's recent transactions |
| `get_playbook` | Step-by-step guides: `getting-started`, `models`, `workflows`, `workflow-graph`, `workflow-agent`, `studio`, `agents`, `billing`, `controls` |
| `search_docs` | Search Wiro documentation |

Prompts: `build_workflow`, `deploy_agent`, `create_with_studio` and
`talk_to_my_agent`. Each one sends the assistant to the matching playbook first.

Paid work: model and workflow runs, Studio and Workflow Agent turns, and
messages to your own agents (from the AI usage the agent's plan includes, then
your Wiro balance) cost money. Before a run or a Studio or Workflow Agent turn,
the assistant tells you the expected cost and waits for your yes. Agent plans and
moves to a larger plan are paid from your Wiro balance and first return a quote
(for a move inside a billing period, the amount Wiro works out for the time left) and act only
when called again with `confirm: true` and `confirm_charge_usd`; if the price
changed, nothing is charged and a new quote comes back. Skill changes cost
nothing, since every plan includes every skill, and a move to a smaller plan
starts with the next renewal, with nothing charged or refunded. Deletions, connecting
an agent to a Wiro project with `bind_agent_project` and graph replacements also
wait for `confirm: true`; a graph replacement's summary shows the old and new
value of each step input that changes. Changes to a spend limit or a Model
Access rule with `manage_spend_limit` and `manage_model_access` also wait for
`confirm: true`, after a summary with the old and new values. No tool adds
funds or takes a card payment: when the balance can't pay a plan, the quote says
how much to add on wiro.ai. `buy_credits` is retired and charges nothing.

Calls through the hosted MCP server count toward the workspace's
[spend limits](/docs/spend-limits) on the `mcp` surface, and calls from the Wiro
browser extensions on the `extension` surface. The
[self-hosted](/docs/mcp-self-hosted) package's calls count on the `api` surface
for now, as calls with its API key. Messages to Studio and the Workflow Agent
count on the `studio` and `workflow-agent` surfaces, and workflow runs on
`workflow`, whichever way they are sent (see
[Surfaces](/docs/tasks#task-surfaces)). When a limit refuses work (error code `93`), the
tool returns an error with Wiro's message and a note: nothing ran and nothing
was charged, and the work should not be tried again until the limit resets or
someone who manages it raises it. `get_controls` shows the limit and when it
resets, and `manage_spend_limit` changes it after a change summary. Limits are
also managed under
[Controls > Spend Limits](https://wiro.ai/panel/controls/spend-limits).

The workspace's [Model Access](/docs/model-access) rules apply to these calls
too, on the same surfaces. A model a rule blocks is refused before anything runs
(error code `92`), and the tool returns an error with Wiro's message, which names
the rule. A message to Studio or the Workflow Agent is refused the same way when
a rule blocks its chat model, the one it names or the default. Nothing ran and
nothing was charged. `check_model_access` shows why
the model is blocked, and `manage_model_access` changes the rule after a change
summary. Rules are also managed under
[Controls > Model Access](https://wiro.ai/panel/controls/model-access).

If a generation exceeds the wait budget, continue with `wait_for_task` using
the returned token. Do not call `run_model` again for the same request.
`task_error` remains non-terminal in Task/Detail; the wait ends only at
`task_postprocess_end` or `task_cancel`.
Workflow runs, agent replies and agent start-up use the same bounded waits:
follow the returned `nextAction` instead of starting the job again.
An LLM model continues a chat only when its schema lists `session_id`: send the
same `session_id` on every turn with the next `prompt`. A turn that ended with
tool calls is continued with `previousTaskToken` and `toolOutputs`.
Tools advertise typed input/output schemas and return `structuredContent` with
stable task states and an executable `nextAction` for reliable LLM chaining.
Every tool that takes arguments refuses an argument it does not know and names
the right one where it can, such as `taskid` for `task_id`; a call that carries
`toolCallId`, a key some clients add on their own, reads only the arguments the
tool takes.
Completed media responses include standard MCP resource links plus an
assistant-audience instruction to render images and preserve clickable media
links in the user-facing response. This works even when a client displays
resource links as tool metadata instead of previewing them inside the tool card.
In the text of a result, an agent's reply, the links taken from it and a
model's answer sit in fenced blocks under fixed labels, apart from the server's
own guidance, so the assistant treats them as content and acts only on the
guidance and `nextAction`.

# Self-Hosted MCP

Run the Wiro MCP server locally on your own machine using npx.

## Quick Start

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "wiro": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@wiro-ai/wiro-mcp@latest"],
      "env": {
        "WIRO_API_KEY": "your-api-key",
        "WIRO_API_SECRET": "your-api-secret"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The self-hosted server exposes the same 56 tools, playbooks and prompts as
the hosted server, including bounded `run_model`, `wait_for_task`, and optional short waits through
`get_task.wait_seconds`. The `@latest` in the npx `args` makes
`npx` look up the newest version on npm at every start, so clients do not
reuse an older cached package.

## Environment Variables

| Variable | Required | Description |
|----------|----------|-------------|
| `WIRO_API_KEY` | Yes | Your Wiro project API key |
| `WIRO_API_SECRET` | No | API secret (for signature auth) |
| `WIRO_API_BASE_URL` | No | Override API URL (default: `https://api.wiro.ai/v1`) |
| `WIRO_TOOLSETS` | No | Comma-separated tool groups to load: `models`, `workflows`, `agents`, `controls` (default: all) |

`get_account`, `get_playbook` and `search_docs` are always available, and
`workflows` also brings the model search tools it needs. The conversation tools
for Studio and the Workflow Agent come with either `workflows` or `agents`, and
`controls` loads the four Controls tools, which come with 1.9.0 and later. The
self-hosted server's calls count on the `api` surface of [spend limits](/docs/spend-limits) and
[Model Access](/docs/model-access) rules for now, as calls with its API key,
except its messages to Studio and the Workflow Agent and its workflow runs,
which count on `studio`, `workflow-agent` and `workflow` (see
[Surfaces](/docs/tasks#task-surfaces)).

## Authentication errors

If the project uses signature-based auth and `WIRO_API_SECRET` is not set, tool calls fail with:

```
Wiro API error 401: This project uses signature-based auth. Set WIRO_API_SECRET to the project's API secret in your MCP server config.
```

Add `WIRO_API_SECRET` to the `env` block of your MCP config and restart the client. The other messages are the same as on the hosted server: see [Authentication errors](/docs/wiro-mcp-server#mcp-auth).

## GitHub & npm

- GitHub: [github.com/wiroai/Wiro-MCP](https://github.com/wiroai/Wiro-MCP)
- npm: [@wiro-ai/wiro-mcp](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@wiro-ai/wiro-mcp)

# Node.js Library

Use Wiro AI models directly in your Node.js or TypeScript projects with a simple API client.

## Overview

The [`@wiro-ai/wiro-mcp`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@wiro-ai/wiro-mcp) package exports a `WiroClient` class that you can use as a standalone API client, with no MCP setup required. It handles authentication, model discovery, execution, task polling, and file uploads.

## Installation

```bash
npm install @wiro-ai/wiro-mcp
```

## Quick Start

```javascript
import { WiroClient } from '@wiro-ai/wiro-mcp/client';

const client = new WiroClient('YOUR_API_KEY', 'YOUR_API_SECRET');

const run = await client.runModel('google/nano-banana-pro', {
  prompt: 'A futuristic city at sunset',
  aspectRatio: '16:9',
  resolution: '2K'
});

const result = await client.waitForTask(run.socketaccesstoken);
const task = result.tasklist[0];

if (task.pexit === '0') {
  console.log('Output:', task.outputs[0].url);
}
```

## Available Methods

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `searchModels(params?)` | Search and browse models by keyword, category, or owner. |
| `getModelSchema(model)` | Get full parameter schema and pricing for a model. |
| `explore()` | Browse curated models organized by category. |
| `runModel(model, params, signal?)` | Run a model. Returns task ID and socket access token. |
| `waitForTask(tasktokenOrReference, timeoutMs?, options?)` | Poll until completion. Default timeout: 120s. Supports abort, progress, and transient retries. |
| `getTask({ tasktoken?, taskid? }, signal?)` | Get current task status and outputs. |
| `cancelTask(tasktokenOrReference, signal?)` | Cancel a queued task using the API-required task ID. |
| `killTask(tasktokenOrReference, signal?)` | Kill a running task using its token or task ID. |
| `listTasks(params?, signal?)` | List the tasks of the key's workspace, newest first. |
| `uploadFile(url, fileName?)` | Upload a file from URL for use as model input. |
| `post(path, body?, signal?)` | Call any other Wiro API endpoint with the same credentials; check `result` on the returned body. |
| `postForm(path, form, signal?)` | Same as `post`, for `multipart/form-data` endpoints. |
| `isOwnApiKey(value)` | Says whether a value is this client's API key, without handing the key out. |

`TaskWaitTimeoutError` preserves the last Task/Detail response. Resume
`waitForTask` with the same identifier instead of calling `runModel` again.

To send headers of your own with every API request, pass `requestHeaders` in
the options (fourth parameter): a function that gets `{ pathname, apiKey }` and
returns a plain object of string values. It cannot set `x-api-key`,
`x-signature`, `x-nonce` or `Content-Type`. It replaces `trustedProxy`, which
was removed in 1.5.0.

# FAQ

Common questions about using the Wiro API.

**How do I get an API key?** Sign up at wiro.ai, then create a project at wiro.ai/panel/project. Copy your API key (and secret, if signature-based) and store them securely. You can see them again on the Projects page after you confirm it's you.

**Which authentication method should I use?** Signature-Based is recommended. API Key Only is simpler. Use either method only from your own server, never in browser or mobile app code.

**Do I pay for failed tasks?** No. Only successfully completed tasks (pexit "0") are billed.

**How do LLM responses work?** LLM models return their response in `outputs` (structured, with `contenttype: "raw"` containing `prompt`, `raw`, `thinking`, `answer`) and as merged text in `debugoutput`.

**Can I send a URL instead of uploading a file?** Yes. For `fileinput` parameters, use the `{id}Url` suffix (e.g., `inputImageUrl`). For `multifileinput`, send comma-separated URLs in the field that puts `Url` before `Multiple` (e.g., `inputDocumentUrlMultiple`). For `combinefileinput`, pass URLs directly in the original parameter. The URL must be a public `http(s)` address. See Model Parameters.

**Does the MCP server cost extra?** No. The [Wiro MCP server](/docs/wiro-mcp-server) is free. You pay the normal prices for the work its tools start: model runs, the model steps of workflow runs, Studio and Workflow Agent turns, and agent plans and the AI usage agents pay from the balance.

**Which other apps have a Wiro AI add-on?** ComfyUI, Dify, WordPress, Obsidian, Figma, Blender, Raycast, Zed, GitHub Actions, Hermes Agent, coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Cursor (agent skills), the Vercel AI SDK (with a Next.js starter for Vercel and Railway), and the Chrome, Edge, Opera, Brave, Firefox and Safari browsers. Each add-on is open source in the [wiroai](https://github.com/wiroai) GitHub organization, with its install steps in the repository. Store listings: the [WordPress plugin directory](https://wordpress.org/plugins/wiro-ai/), [Obsidian community plugins](https://community.obsidian.md/plugins/wiro-ai), the [Comfy Registry](https://registry.comfy.org/nodes/comfyui-wiro), the [Chrome Web Store](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/wiro-ai-tools-for-images/cehkhdmppbnfeahegjjkdhangjelehab), [Microsoft Edge Add-ons](https://microsoftedge.microsoft.com/addons/detail/wiro-ai-tools-for-images/obkibkhehpojlejdoinhlmoofalgaddg), [Firefox Add-ons](https://addons.mozilla.org/firefox/addon/wiro-ai/) and the [Naver Whale Store](https://store.whale.naver.com/detail/elgobhnkemhlhfakdmpijbknhehnkgle); the n8n node is [verified by n8n](https://n8n.io/integrations/wiro-ai/). AI assistants connect through the [Wiro MCP server](/docs/wiro-mcp-server).

**Can I use a webhook instead of polling?** Yes. All models support an optional `callbackUrl` parameter. It must be a public `http(s)` address.

**What are Wiro Agents?** Wiro Agents are autonomous AI assistants that you deploy and manage via the API. Unlike single model runs, agents can connect to third-party services (Twitter, Google Ads, HubSpot, etc.), maintain conversation memory across sessions, and run scheduled tasks automatically. See the [Agent Overview](/docs/agent-overview) for details.

**How do I deploy an agent?** Pick a template in the [agent catalog](https://wiro.ai/agents) or build your own, then call `POST /UserAgent/Deploy` with `useprepaid: true` and a plan in `tier`: `starter` ($5 a month), `pro` ($30) or `max` ($100), each including its own price in AI usage a month. Your Wiro balance pays the plan, and Wiro queues the agent to start on its own. Then connect the services it uses. Every plan includes every skill and connector. See [Agent Overview](/docs/agent-overview) for the full lifecycle.

**How much does an agent cost?** Each agent runs on one of three monthly plans: Starter ($5 a month), Pro ($30) or Max ($100), each paid from your Wiro balance and including its own price in AI usage: Pro includes $30 of AI usage a month. Every plan includes every skill and connector, so turning one on or off costs nothing. Each turn the agent runs is priced by the tokens its model uses; once the included usage is used up, the agent uses your Wiro balance, the same balance model runs use, and a new turn needs at least $0.50 there. A higher plan starts at once; a lower plan starts at the next renewal. See [Pricing Model](/docs/agent-overview#pricing-model-plans-ai-usage-balance).

**How much disk space does my agent have?** Starter gives an agent 250 MB, Pro 500 MB and Max 1 GB for its files: the workspace, generated media and temporary files. Chat history and system files don't count. Downloads and temporary files outside the workspace are cleared when the agent restarts, and when they pass 1 GB. When the disk is full, the agent can't save new files until some are deleted or it moves to a bigger plan. `UserAgent/Detail` shows the usage in `disk`. See [Disk Space](/docs/agent-overview#disk-space).

**Can I build my own product with Wiro Agents?** Yes. Use the Agent Messaging API to send messages programmatically, receive streaming responses via WebSocket, and get async notifications via webhooks. You can build white-label chat interfaces, webhook-driven pipelines, and multi-agent workflows. See [Agent Use Cases](/docs/agent-use-cases). For a chat in your own product, with setup from chat, follow [Agent Chat Integration](/docs/agent-chat-integration).

**Can I watch my agent work?** Yes. In the Wiro panel, the people who manage an agent can open its Screen beside the chat and watch its computer live (on a team agent, while its Chat Mode is Collaborative). The owner of a personal agent that has never been in a team, or whose browser was reset after it last left one, can also take control and use the keyboard and mouse, for example to sign in to a site for the agent. Products built on the API can show the same Screen, and Take Control, in their own app and decide which of their users see it; the agent's `screen` setting turns it off for everyone. See [Screen and Take Control](/docs/agent-overview#screen-and-take-control) and [Screen and Take Control in Your App](/docs/agent-chat-integration#screen-and-take-control-in-your-app).

**How do I connect third-party services to an agent?** Agents connect to services like X, Instagram, Google Ads, and HubSpot through connectors, with your customer's own API keys or the vendor's sign-in. Browse them with `POST /AgentConnector/List` and connect one with `POST /UserAgent/ConnectorConnect`. See [Agent Connectors](/docs/agent-connectors). You can also ask the agent in its chat: it proposes a setup card, and an agent admin approves it and gives the key, which the agent never sees. See [Setup From Chat](/docs/agent-messaging#setup-from-chat).

**What happens when I delete my account?** Your account is closed right away and its API keys stop working. Its subscriptions stop renewing and end with their current billing period, without a refund. A renewal invoice that is still unpaid is cancelled. Its automatic top-ups stop. 30 days later, or later if something still needs it, such as an active subscription, we permanently delete its data, including your files, tasks, projects and API keys. Until then, write to [support@wiro.ai](mailto:support@wiro.ai) if you want it restored. We keep records the law requires, such as payment and invoice records. See [Data Deletion](https://wiro.ai/agreement/data-deletion) for details.

# n8n Wiro Integration

Run any Wiro AI model from your n8n workflows: video, image, audio, LLM, 3D, and more.

The **Wiro AI** community node (`@wiro-ai/n8n-nodes-wiro`) runs any model in the Wiro AI catalog from a single node. Pick a model from a searchable list and its inputs load into the node with their default values. **Model > Run** starts a task and returns its output files (`url`, `urls`) or a text model's reply (`text`), with `taskId`, `status`, `costUsd` and `elapsedSeconds`. **Task > Get** and **Task > Wait** read a task by its ID. The node also works as a tool for an n8n AI Agent, and takes a **Wiro AI API** credential: your project's API key, plus the API secret if the project uses signature authentication.

## Installation

The node is [verified by n8n](https://n8n.io/integrations/wiro-ai/): an instance owner can search for **Wiro AI** in the nodes panel of the workflow editor and install it, on n8n Cloud and on self-hosted instances that show verified community nodes.

Install via n8n UI: **Settings → Community Nodes → Install → `@wiro-ai/n8n-nodes-wiro`**

Or via command line: `npm install @wiro-ai/n8n-nodes-wiro`

## Links

- [npm: @wiro-ai/n8n-nodes-wiro](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@wiro-ai/n8n-nodes-wiro)
- [GitHub: wiroai/n8n-nodes-wiro](https://github.com/wiroai/n8n-nodes-wiro)
- [n8n: Wiro AI integration (verified)](https://n8n.io/integrations/wiro-ai/)

# Workflows

Chain models and built-in steps into one graph, save it, and run it again with new inputs.

## Overview

A workflow is a saved chain of steps. Each step runs one Wiro model or one built-in utility. The Start node holds the inputs people fill in, and the End node lists the results. A saved workflow runs each time someone starts it, on [wiro.ai/workflows](https://wiro.ai/workflows) or through the API.

The `/Workflow/*` endpoints list and read workflows, save new ones from a graph, edit, clone and delete them, run them and follow their runs. To design a workflow in plain language, use the [Workflow Agent](/docs/workflow-agent). The [Wiro MCP Server](/docs/wiro-mcp-server) offers these endpoints as tools for AI assistants.

### Authentication

Every `/Workflow/*` route on this page takes a project API key: `x-api-key`, plus `x-nonce` and `x-signature` for a project that uses signature authentication (see [Authentication](/docs/authentication)). A key acts as the person who created its project, in that project's workspace.

### Workspaces and the gallery

- A workflow belongs to the workspace it was created in: personal, or a team. Another workspace cannot read, run or change it, unless it is published in the public gallery: anyone can read and run a published workflow.
- A **protected** workflow hides its steps from people outside its owner's workspace. They can still see its inputs and outputs and run it.
- Workflows saved through the API are private. Publishing to the gallery happens on wiro.ai, and a published workflow goes through review again after its title, description, tags or steps change.

### Slugs

A workflow is named by its full slug: its `slug`, a dash and its 5-character `slugid`, such as `product-shots-a1B2c`. Every endpoint that takes a workflow takes the full slug as `slug`. The workflow's page is `https://wiro.ai/workflows/<full slug>`.

## The Workflow Graph

A workflow's definition is one JSON object, its `contents`. It holds the steps, the Start fields people fill in and the End node that lists the results. Before you save a graph you wrote yourself, prepare it with [Workflow/Prepare](#post-workflowprepare): it checks the graph against the live model catalog and fills in what the Wiro editor would.

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `version` | string | Always `"1"`. |
| `nodes` | object | The steps, keyed by step id, plus the End node under the key `output`. The Start node is not in `nodes`. |
| `schema.input` | object | The Start fields, keyed by the input names a run takes. |
| `schema.output` | object | Always `{}`. |
| `output` | object | A copy of the End node's `fields`. |
| `metadata.input.position` | object | Where the Start node sits on the canvas, such as `{ "x": 0, "y": 0 }`. |
| `metadata.input.values` | object | Optional saved values for the Start fields. A run uses them for the fields it leaves out. |

[Workflow/Prepare](#post-workflowprepare) accepts a graph of at most 40 KB of JSON (40,960 bytes), and counts it again after it fills each step's defaults.

### Steps

Each step is `"node-<id>": { "id", "type", "tool", "depends", "input", "metadata" }`.

- The key is `node-` followed by 1 to 64 letters, digits, `-` or `_`. `id` repeats the key exactly, and `type` is `"run"`.
- `tool` is a model slug (`owner/model`) or a built-in utility: `workflow-utilities/output-filter`, `workflow-utilities/merge-text` or `workflow-utilities/split-text`.
- `input` maps the tool's parameter ids, from [Tool/Detail](/docs/models), to values: fixed values, or references to Start fields and earlier steps.
- `depends` lists every source the step reads: `"input"` when it uses a Start field, and the id of each step it references. No duplicates, never the step itself, never `"output"`.
- `metadata.position` is `{ "x": number, "y": number }` and only places the step on the canvas.

### Start fields

Each key in `schema.input` is that input's name at run time. Give each field `label`, `type`, `defaultValue` and `ui` (an object); [Workflow/Prepare](#post-workflowprepare) fills in the rest the way the editor does. wiro.ai titles each field with its key in the run form, so use a short readable key such as `product_photo`.

- **Text:** `"type": "string"` with `"ui": { "field": "textarea" }`.
- **Choice list:** `"type": "string"` with `"ui": { "field": "select", "options": [{ "value": "16:9", "text": "Wide" }] }`.
- **Number:** `"type": "number"` (whole) or `"float"` (decimal). **Yes or no:** `"type": "boolean"`. Both with `"ui": {}`.
- **File:** `"type": "string"` with `"ui": { "field": "image" }`, or `"audio"`, `"video"` or `"pdf"`. The value is a public URL.

A Start field that the End node or a step leading to it uses, with no saved value and no default, must get a value when the workflow runs. [Workflow/Detail](#post-workflowdetail) names these fields in `requiredinputs`.

### References

- `$input.<key>` is the value of a Start field.
- `$node-<id>.outputs` is everything a model step produced: its files, or an LLM step's reply.
- `$node-<id>.result` is the result of `output-filter` or `merge-text`. `$node-<id>.text1` to `.textN` are the parts produced by `split-text`.

A reference must be the whole string value, or one whole item of an array. It is never filled in inside longer text, and a fixed value that starts with `$` is read as a reference. To put a Start field or an LLM answer inside a prompt, join the parts with `merge-text`, such as `"texts": ["Write a caption for:", "$input.name"]`, and reference its `result`.

When a model step's outputs feed another model, a single file parameter takes the first file, a combined file parameter (`combinefileinput`) takes all of the files, and a text parameter takes the first file URL or the LLM's answer.

### The End node

It is `"output": { "id": "output", "type": "display", "depends", "input": {}, "fields", "metadata" }`.

- `fields` maps each result name to one reference. Give each result its own source.
- `depends` lists the steps the fields read from. It cannot be empty: a workflow with nothing wired to its End node cannot run.
- The top-level `output` must equal `fields`. Steps that do not lead to the End node never run.

### Built-in utilities

Utilities are free and finish at once. [Workflow/UtilityDetail](#post-workflowutilitydetail) returns their parameters and output ports.

- **`output-filter`** picks items from a model step. Its `outputs` parameter must be a `$node-<id>.outputs` reference. With `mode` `"file"` it keeps the files that match `contenttype` (such as `"image"`, `"audio/*"` or `"mp3"`) and `name`, up to `count` items (default 1). With `mode` `"llm"` it takes `field` (`"answer"`, `"thinking"`, `"raw"` or `"prompt"`) from an LLM step. Port: `result`.
- **`merge-text`** joins `texts` (an array of references or fixed strings) with `separator` (default a space), skipping empty items unless `skipEmpty` is `false`. Port: `result`.
- **`split-text`** splits `text` by `separator` (default a new line) into `count` parts, 2 to 10 (default 5). `count` must be a fixed value. Ports: `text1` to `textN`.

Other operations, such as joining videos or adding a voice track to a video, are ordinary models in the catalog.

### Model steps

- Use only parameter ids from the model's [Tool/Detail](/docs/models).
- Set every parameter you care about. A parameter you leave out takes the model's default from [Tool/Detail](/docs/models). To leave a file parameter empty, set it to `[]`, or `""` for a single file.
- A single file parameter takes one URL string. A combined file parameter (`combinefileinput`) takes an array, even for one file. A multi-file parameter (`multifileinput`) takes its URLs comma-separated in its matching `...UrlMultiple` field.
- Take each value, such as a duration, a size or an option, from the model's schema in [Tool/Detail](/docs/models).
- Training models cannot be used in workflows.

### A minimal workflow

One text input, one image model and one result. Replace `owner/model` with a real model and `prompt` with that model's text parameter id.

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "nodes": {
    "node-image": {
      "id": "node-image", "type": "run", "tool": "owner/model", "depends": ["input"],
      "input": { "prompt": "$input.prompt" },
      "metadata": { "position": { "x": 350, "y": 0 } }
    },
    "output": {
      "id": "output", "type": "display", "depends": ["node-image"], "input": {},
      "fields": { "image": "$node-image.outputs" },
      "metadata": { "position": { "x": 700, "y": 0 } }
    }
  },
  "output": { "image": "$node-image.outputs" },
  "schema": {
    "input": {
      "prompt": { "label": "Prompt", "type": "string", "defaultValue": "", "ui": { "field": "textarea" } }
    },
    "output": {}
  },
  "metadata": { "input": { "position": { "x": 0, "y": 0 } } }
}
```

To turn that image into a video, add a second model step that reads the first step's file and a `motion` Start field:

```json
"node-video": {
  "id": "node-video", "type": "run", "tool": "owner/video-model",
  "depends": ["input", "node-image"],
  "input": { "inputImage": "$node-image.outputs", "prompt": "$input.motion" },
  "metadata": { "position": { "x": 700, "y": 0 } }
}
```

Then set the End node's `"depends": ["node-video"]` and `"fields": { "video": "$node-video.outputs" }`, copy those fields to the top-level `output`, and move the End node to `"x": 1050`. `inputImage` stands for the video model's image parameter: check its real id in the model's schema.

## How a Run Works

[Workflow/Run](#post-workflowrun) answers at once with a run token, the `workflowtoken`; the steps run after that. Read the run with [Workflow/RunDetail](#post-workflowrundetail) until its `status` is final.

- Only the steps that lead to the End node run. Steps run in layers: a step that depends on no other step is in the first layer, and any other step is one layer after the latest of the steps it depends on. The steps of a layer start together, and the next layer starts once every step of the current one has finished.
- When a step fails, every step in a later layer is skipped, on every branch, and the run ends as `failed`.
- Check the expected cost (see [Costs](#costs)) before you start a run.
- The run belongs to the caller's workspace and is paid from that workspace's wallet, also when the workflow is a public one from another workspace.

### Run statuses

| Status | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `running` | Steps are queued or running. |
| `completed` | Every step finished. The End node's fields hold the results. |
| `failed` | A step failed, and the steps after it were skipped. |
| `stopped` | The run reached its breakpoint. Continue it with [RunResume](#post-workflowrunresume). |
| `cancelled` | One of the run's steps was cancelled. |

A step is `pending`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled` or `aborted` (skipped because an earlier step failed). A failed step's `cause` is `tool-error` (the model refused its inputs or the task failed; `error` says why), `poll-timeout` (the step ran past 4 hours and was not charged), `spend-limit-reached` (a [spend limit](/docs/spend-limits) refused the step before it started; `error` holds the limit's message), or another short code.

### Breakpoints

To test the first steps, start the run with `breakpointNodeId`. The run executes every layer up to and including the one that holds that step, then ends as `stopped`, and the steps after it stay `pending`. The breakpoint must be a step the run executes and cannot be in the last layer. Only people who can edit the workflow can set one. Check the outputs, then continue with [RunResume](#post-workflowrunresume), to the end or to a later breakpoint.

### Resuming

[RunResume](#post-workflowrunresume) continues a `failed` or `stopped` run on the same `workflowtoken`. Completed steps keep their outputs and are not charged again. Failed, skipped and not yet run steps run again as new tasks, billed to the wallet that paid for the run.

A resume runs the remaining steps exactly as the run started them, with the same inputs and settings: changes saved to the workflow since then apply to new runs only. So resume after a temporary failure, such as a timeout or a model that asked to try again later. An error about a parameter value, a file or a limit such as duration or size comes from the inputs or the settings: fix them and start a new run.

## Costs

- Saving, reading, preparing, cloning and deleting workflows is free.
- Nothing is charged when a run starts. Each model step is a normal [model task](/docs/run-a-model), billed when it finishes successfully at that model's price. Failed steps are not charged, and utility steps are free.
- To start, the wallet must hold $0.50 for each model step the run will execute (up to the breakpoint, when one is set). Otherwise the run is refused with code `97`, `Insufficient balance`. The [concurrency limit](/docs/concurrency-limits) also applies (code `96`).
- The expected cost of a run is the sum of the model prices for the settings each step uses, from [Tool/Detail](/docs/models). A run's `totalcost` shows the list price of the steps finished so far, and once the run has ended `chargedcost` and `discountamount` show what the wallet paid. `chargedcost` is `null` while a step's charge is still settling.
- The workspace's [spend limits](/docs/spend-limits) apply when a run starts or resumes, and again before each step starts. A run is refused with code `93` when its known price would go over a limit that covers it, or once that limit has no room left. Each step is checked the same way with its own price, and holds that price until it is charged. A step a limit refuses fails with cause `spend-limit-reached`, and the run ends as `failed`: resume it with [RunResume](#post-workflowrunresume) once the limit allows.
- The workspace's [Model Access](/docs/model-access) rules apply when a run starts or resumes: when a rule blocks the model of a step that will run, the run is refused with code `92` before anything runs, and the message names that model. When the workflow's steps are hidden from you, as on a protected workflow from another workspace, the message names your rule but not the model, for example `Your account can't use one of the models this workflow runs. Model Access rules decide which models can run.` Steps that will not run, such as the steps after a breakpoint, are not checked.
- A run, its resumes and every step it runs count on the `workflow` [surface](/docs/tasks#task-surfaces) of spend limits and Model Access, whether you start it with an API key, through MCP or in the dashboard, and each step's task has `surface` `workflow`. A run that a deployed agent, Studio or the Workflow Agent starts keeps that surface instead. Before workflows had their own surface, a run counted on the surface it was started from, such as `api`.

## **POST** /Workflow/List

Lists the workflows of the key's workspace, or searches the public gallery.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `scope` | string | No | `"my"` (default) for the key's workspace, `"public"` for the public gallery. |
| `search` | string | No | Text to look for in the slug, title, description or tags. |
| `sort` | string | No | `my`: `createtime` (default), `updatetime` or `title`. `public`: `createtime` (default), `runcount`, `likecount`, `clonecount` or `ratingscore`. |
| `order` | string | No | `DESC` (default) or `ASC`. |
| `start` | number | No | Offset for paging. Default `0`. |
| `limit` | number | No | Rows per page. `my`: default `20`, maximum `1000`. `public`: default `50`, maximum `200`. |
| `ispublic` | string | No | `my` only: `"0"` for private workflows, `"1"` for workflows submitted to the gallery. |
| `tags` | array | No | `public` only: workflows with any of these tags, up to 20. |
| `model` | string | No | `public` only: workflows that use this model, as `"owner/model"`. |
| `onlyfavorites` | string | No | `public` only: `"1"` for the workflows you liked. |
| `toolpreview` | string | No | `public` only: `"1"` adds `toolitems`, the models each workflow uses with their titles and covers. |

The response is `{ "result": true, "errors": [], "workflow": [...], "total": 1 }`. In your workspace (`my`), a personal key lists your own workflows and a team key lists every workflow of the team.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `id` | The workflow's numeric id. |
| `slug`, `slugid` | The full slug is `<slug>-<slugid>`. |
| `title`, `description`, `tags`, `cover` | The workflow's details. |
| `ispublic` | `1` when the workflow was submitted to the gallery. |
| `status` | `null` when never published, `1` waiting for review, `2` listed in the gallery, `3` rejected. |
| `isprotected` | `1` when the steps are hidden from people outside the owner's workspace. |
| `clonedfromid` | On a clone, the id of the workflow it was copied from. |
| `stepcount`, `toolcount`, `utilitycount` | The number of steps, model steps and utility steps. |
| `teamname` | The team the workflow belongs to, if any. |
| `runcount`, `likecount`, `clonecount`, `ratingaverage`, `ratingcount`, `commentcount` | Gallery counters. `runcount` counts runs while the workflow is listed. |
| `createtime`, `updatetime` | Unix seconds. Pass `updatetime` to [Update](#post-workflowupdate) as `loadedUpdatetime`. |

Gallery rows (`public`) also carry `tools` (the models the workflow uses; `null` on a protected workflow) and `user` (`username`, `avatar`) for the creator.

### Response

```json
{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "workflow": [
    {
      "id": 1842,
      "slug": "product-ad",
      "slugid": "a1B2c",
      "title": "Product ad",
      "description": "Turns a product photo into a short ad video",
      "tags": ["ads", "video"],
      "cover": null,
      "ispublic": 0,
      "status": null,
      "isprotected": 0,
      "clonedfromid": null,
      "stepcount": 2,
      "toolcount": 2,
      "utilitycount": 0,
      "teamname": null,
      "runcount": 0,
      "likecount": 0,
      "clonecount": 0,
      "ratingaverage": null,
      "ratingcount": 0,
      "commentcount": 0,
      "createtime": "1761901200",
      "updatetime": "1761901200"
    }
  ],
  "total": 1
}
```

## **POST** /Workflow/Detail

Returns one workflow with its graph.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `slug` | string | Yes | The full slug, such as `product-ad-a1B2c`. |

The response is `{ "result": true, "errors": [], "workflow": [ { ... } ] }`: the fields of List plus `contents`, the graph as an object (see [The Workflow Graph](#the-workflow-graph)). Its `schema.input` lists the inputs a run takes, and `metadata.input.values` the saved values.

- `requiredinputs` lists the Start fields a run must be given: the ones used by the End node or by a step leading to it that have no saved value and no default. An empty array means a run needs no input. Read this list to decide what to ask for; a field's `required` flag in `schema.input` doesn't decide it. On a protected workflow from another workspace, a run doesn't use the creator's saved values, so only a default takes a field off the list.
- A workflow from your workspace, or one published in the gallery, can be read. A private workflow of another workspace answers `This workflow does not belong to your current workspace.` or `You don't have any permission for this action.`, and a clone can only be read by its owner's workspace.
- A protected workflow read from outside its owner's workspace comes back with its steps removed: `contents` keeps only the Start fields and the End node, and `estimatedcost` gives an estimate of one run, `{ "type": "estimated", "value": 0.42 }` (`"unavailable"` with `value: null` when it cannot be estimated).
- `rejectreason` is present only for the workflow's own workspace: on a rejected workflow it says why.
- A deleted or unknown workflow answers `Workflow not found`.

Saved Start values are part of the workflow: everyone who can read it sees them, the gallery too once it is published, and clones keep them. Never save a key, token or password there. Model steps are billed to the Wiro wallet and need no key from the model's provider.

## **POST** /Workflow/Prepare

Prepares a graph you wrote for saving, the way the Wiro editor does: it checks every step against the live model catalog, fills each model parameter you left out with its default, completes the Start fields and the End node, and lays the steps out. It writes and charges nothing. Prepare the graph, then save the prepared `contents` with [Add](#post-workflowadd) or [Update](#post-workflowupdate).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `contents` | object | Yes | The graph, as an object or a JSON string. |
| `mode` | string | No | `"create"` (default) lays every step out again, for a new workflow. `"apply"` keeps the positions you sent, for a change to an existing workflow; every step then needs a numeric position. |
| `anchorNodeIds` | array | No | `apply` only: step ids (`"input"` for Start, `"output"` for End) that keep their exact positions; the other steps move down until nothing overlaps. |

On success, `contents` is the prepared graph. On failure, `result` is `false` and `issues` lists every problem at once, each `{ code, message, nodeId, input }`: `nodeId` is the step (`"input"` for a Start field, `"output"` for an End field) and `input` the parameter or field. `warnings` can come back either way; `required-input-missing` means a Start field a step uses has no default, so every run must send a value for it.

```json
{
  "result": false,
  "errors": [{ "code": 0, "message": "...", "time": 1761901200 }],
  "issues": [
    { "code": "unknown-input", "message": "...", "nodeId": "node-image", "input": "promt" },
    { "code": "contents-too-large", "message": "Workflow JSON exceeds the 40960-byte limit.", "bytes": 52114, "limit": 40960 }
  ],
  "warnings": []
}
```

Common issue codes: `tool-not-found` and `tool-not-marketplace` (the model does not exist or is not public), `unknown-input` (a parameter id the model does not have), `unknown-input-reference`, `unknown-node-reference` and `reference-missing-dependency` (a reference to a missing Start field or step, or one not listed in `depends`), `embedded-workflow-reference` (a reference inside longer text), `file-input-not-array` and `single-file-only` (one file where an array is needed, or the reverse), `request-parameter-required` (a required model parameter has no value), `param-out-of-bounds`, `cycle-detected`, `workflow-has-no-reachable-nodes`, `duplicate-end-reference`, and `contents-too-large` or `prepared-contents-too-large` with `bytes` and `limit`.

Prepare fills every model parameter you leave out with the model's default: compare the prepared step inputs with what you sent, and set or empty the ones you did not mean to keep.

## **POST** /Workflow/Add

Saves a new, private workflow in the key's workspace.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `title` | string | Yes | The workflow's title. If the workspace already has a workflow with this title, a number is added, such as `Product ad-2`. |
| `slug` | string | Yes | The title part of the slug: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, such as `product-ad`. Wiro adds the 5-character `slugid`. |
| `contents` | string | Yes | The prepared graph as a JSON string. |
| `description` | string | No | What the workflow does and what people should put in its inputs. |
| `tags` | string | No | A JSON string of an array of tags, such as `"[\"ads\",\"video\"]"`. Tags that start with `wiro-` are reserved. |

The response is `{ "result": true, "errors": [], "workflow": [ { ... } ] }` with the saved workflow, including its `slugid` and `updatetime`. Add checks that every model and utility exists; run the graph through [Prepare](#post-workflowprepare) first, which checks the references, the inputs and everything else a run needs.

## **POST** /Workflow/Update

Changes a workflow of the key's workspace.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `slug` | string | Yes | The full slug. |
| `title` | string | No | A new title. |
| `description` | string | No | A new description. |
| `tags` | string | No | A JSON string of the new tag array. Keep any `wiro-` tags the workflow already has. |
| `contents` | string | No | A new graph as a JSON string, prepared with `mode: "apply"`. It replaces the old one. |
| `loadedUpdatetime` | string | No | The `updatetime` you read. If someone saved the workflow since then, nothing is written. |
| `force` | boolean | No | `true` saves even when `loadedUpdatetime` no longer matches. |
| `input` | object | No | Protected clones only: new saved values for the Start fields, by key. |

Title and description are changed only when you send a non-empty value. The response holds the workflow after the change, with its new `updatetime`.

- **Concurrent edits.** When `loadedUpdatetime` no longer matches, the update is refused with `This workflow was modified by another user. Reload to see latest changes or save to overwrite.` and the response carries `currentUpdatetime`. Read the workflow again and redo the change on top, or send `force: true` to overwrite.
- **Published workflows.** Changing the title, description, tags or graph of a workflow in the gallery sends it back to review, and it leaves the gallery until it is approved again.
- **Clones.** A clone of a protected workflow keeps its steps hidden: you can change its title, description and tags, and its saved Start values with `input`, but not its `contents`.
- When a new graph stops using files that were uploaded into the workflow in the wiro.ai editor, those files are deleted, unless a past run or a clone still uses them.

## **POST** /Workflow/Clone

Copies a workflow from the public gallery into the key's workspace.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `slug` | string | Yes | The full slug of a workflow listed in the gallery. |

The copy is private and free. It keeps the graph and the saved Start values; a taken title becomes `Title-Clone`. The response holds the new workflow, without `contents`: read it with [Detail](#post-workflowdetail). Each call makes another copy.

- Only a workflow listed in the gallery can be cloned (`This workflow cannot be cloned`), and not into the workspace it already belongs to (`This workflow already belongs to this workspace`).
- A clone can never be published or cloned again, and only its own workspace can read it.
- A clone of a protected workflow keeps its steps hidden from everyone, its owner included. It can still be run.

## **POST** /Workflow/Delete

Deletes a workflow of the key's workspace. It leaves every list and the gallery and can no longer be run or read. Runs already started finish, and clones keep working.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `slug` | string | Yes | The full slug. |

The response is `{ "result": true, "errors": [], "workflow": [] }`. There is no undo.

## **POST** /Workflow/Run

Starts a run and answers at once with its token.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `slug` | string | Yes | The full slug. |
| `input` | object | No | Values for the Start fields, keyed as in `schema.input`: strings, numbers, booleans or arrays. Files are public URLs. A field you leave out uses its saved value, then its default. |
| `breakpointNodeId` | string | No | A step id to stop after (see [Breakpoints](#breakpoints)). |

```json
{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "workflowtoken": "Lk3vQ9xT2mWc7Rp4Yh8Nd1Fs6Gb0Zj"
}
```

- Your own workspace's workflows and the workflows listed in the gallery can be run. On a protected gallery workflow from another workspace, a field you leave out uses its default, not the creator's saved value.
- An unknown input key is refused with `Unknown input field(s): <keys>. Check your workflow's Start Node schema for valid field names.`, and a Start field that a step needs and that has no value is refused with `A required input value is missing: <key>.`
- Missing inputs and broken references are all returned at once, and nothing is charged for a refused run.
- File inputs are fetched from public http(s) URLs, up to about 100 MB each.

## **POST** /Workflow/RunDetail

Returns a run and its steps. Call it until `status` is `completed`, `failed`, `stopped` or `cancelled`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `workflowtoken` | string | Yes | The run token. |

The response has `workflowrun` and `workflowrunnodes`. Runs are private: the person who started a run can read it, and in a team workspace every member of the team can.

| `workflowrun` field | Description |
|---------------------|-------------|
| `workflowtoken`, `workflowslug` | The run token and the workflow's full slug. |
| `status` | `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `stopped` or `cancelled`. |
| `outcome` | The final status, once the run has ended. |
| `canresume` | `true` when you can continue this run with [RunResume](#post-workflowrunresume). |
| `breakpointnodeid` | The breakpoint in effect, or `null`. |
| `contents` | The graph as this run started it, with the Start values it used. |
| `totalcost` | The list price of the steps finished so far, in USD. |
| `chargedcost`, `discountamount` | Once the run has ended: what the wallet paid and the discount. `null` while a charge is still settling. |
| `startedAt` | Start time in milliseconds. `resumedAt` is added when the run was resumed. |
| `elapsedseconds` | Running time, summed over resumes. |
| `failedNodeCount`, `abortedNodeCount`, `cancelledNodeCount` | Step counts. |

| `workflowrunnodes` field | Description |
|--------------------------|-------------|
| `nodeId`, `tool`, `kind` | The step id, its model or utility, and `tool` or `utility`. |
| `layerIdx` | The step's layer, from 0. |
| `status` | `pending`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled` or `aborted`. |
| `cause`, `error` | Why the step did not complete. |
| `tasktoken` | For a model step that started a task. Pass it to [RunNodeDetail](#post-workflowrunnodedetail). |
| `outputs` | A model step's results: files with `url`, `name`, `contenttype` and `size`, or an LLM's reply as `{ "contenttype": "raw", "content": { "answer": [...] } }`. A utility step's ports, such as `{ "result": [...] }`. A file entry carries no `path` or `mntpath`: use its `url`. |
| `elapsedseconds` | How long the step ran. |

To find a run's results, read the End node's `fields` in `contents` and take the `outputs` of the steps they reference.

When the workflow's steps are hidden from you, as on a protected workflow from another workspace, the run comes back with `graphmasked: true`: `contents` shows only the Start fields and the End node, and `workflowrunnodes` holds only the steps the End node shows, with their `status` and `outputs`.

### Response

```json
{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "workflowrun": {
    "workflowtoken": "Lk3vQ9xT2mWc7Rp4Yh8Nd1Fs6Gb0Zj",
    "workflowslug": "product-ad-a1B2c",
    "status": "completed",
    "outcome": "completed",
    "breakpointnodeid": null,
    "startedAt": 1761902400000,
    "elapsedseconds": 74,
    "totalcost": "0.84",
    "chargedcost": "0.84",
    "discountamount": "0",
    "failedNodeCount": 0,
    "abortedNodeCount": 0,
    "cancelledNodeCount": 0,
    "contents": { "...": "..." }
  },
  "workflowrunnodes": [
    {
      "nodeId": "node-image",
      "tool": "google/nano-banana-pro",
      "kind": "tool",
      "layerIdx": 0,
      "status": "completed",
      "cause": null,
      "error": null,
      "tasktoken": "Ab12Cd34Ef56Gh78Ij90Kl12Mn34Op",
      "outputs": [
        {
          "url": "https://cdn1.wiro.ai/5e8d7a1c/product.png",
          "name": "product.png",
          "contenttype": "image/png",
          "size": "1843212"
        }
      ],
      "elapsedseconds": 31
    },
    {
      "nodeId": "node-video",
      "tool": "klingai/kling-v3",
      "kind": "tool",
      "layerIdx": 1,
      "status": "completed",

      "outputs": [
        {
          "url": "https://cdn1.wiro.ai/9b2f4e6a/ad.mp4",
          "name": "ad.mp4",
          "contenttype": "video/mp4",

        }
```

## **POST** /Workflow/RunNodeDetail

Shows what one model step received and returned, to debug a failed step.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `tasktoken` | string | Yes | The step's `tasktoken` from RunDetail. |

The response's `workflowrunnode` has the step's RunDetail fields plus `taskDetail`: the `parameters` the model received, its `debugoutput`, `taskStatus`, and `modelslugowner` and `modelslugproject`. Utility steps have no task to read. When the workflow's steps are hidden from you, it answers `You don't have any permission for this action.`

## **POST** /Workflow/RunHistory

Lists runs, newest first. A personal key lists your own runs; a team key lists the runs of every member of the team. Runs started on wiro.ai are included.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `start` | number | No | Offset. Default `0`. |
| `limit` | number | No | Default `20`, maximum `1000`. |
| `status` | string | No | `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `stopped` or `cancelled`. |
| `search` | string | No | Text in the workflow's title, or its slug without the 5-character id: `product-ad` finds the runs of `product-ad-a1B2c`. |
| `workflowid` | number | No | Only the runs of this workflow id. |
| `sort` | string | No | `id` (default), `starttime`, `status` or `totalcost`. |
| `order` | string | No | `DESC` (default) or `ASC`. |

The response is `{ "result": true, "errors": [], "workflowruns": [...], "total": 12 }`. Each row has the `workflowrun` fields of [RunDetail](#post-workflowrundetail) without `contents`, plus `workflowid`, `workflowtitle`, `teamname` and `nodes`, each step's `{ nodeId, tool, kind, layerIdx, status }`. To read a run's outputs, call RunDetail with its token.

## **POST** /Workflow/RunResume

Continues a `failed` or `stopped` run on the same token. See [Resuming](#resuming).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `workflowtoken` | string | Yes | The run token. |
| `breakpointNodeId` | string | No | A new breakpoint. Send `null` to run to the end. Leave the field out and a failed run keeps the breakpoint it started with, while a stopped run runs to the end. |

The response is `{ "result": true, "errors": [], "workflowtoken": "..." }`; follow the run with RunDetail again.

- The person who started the run can resume it after a failure. Continuing a stopped run, and setting a breakpoint, needs someone who can edit the workflow; in a team workspace any such member can.
- The balance check runs again for the steps that will run.
- `This run is already resuming or still wrapping up. Try again in a moment` and `A step of this run is still finishing. Try again in a few minutes` mean an earlier step is still settling: wait a few minutes and try once more.
- Any other status is refused with `Only a failed or stopped run can be resumed`.

## **POST** /Workflow/UtilityDetail

Returns a built-in utility's parameters and output ports, in the same shape as a model's parameters in [Tool/Detail](/docs/models).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `slug` | string | Yes | `workflow-utilities/output-filter`, `workflow-utilities/merge-text` or `workflow-utilities/split-text`. |

The response's `utility` holds one entry with `slug`, `title`, `description`, `parameters` (groups of parameter definitions with `id`, `type`, `label`, `defaultvalue`, `options`, `minvalue` and `maxvalue`) and `outputs`, the ports, each `{ id, label, type }`.

## Errors

Business errors come back with HTTP 200, `result: false` and an `errors` array, as everywhere in the Wiro API. The ones you will see most:

| Message | Code | When |
|---------|------|------|
| `Workflow not found` | 0 | An unknown or deleted workflow. |
| `This workflow does not belong to your current workspace.` | 0 | A private workflow of another workspace. Use a key from a project in the workflow's workspace. |
| `You don't have any permission for this action.` | 0 | The key's project creator has no rights on this workflow or run. |
| `You must be a member of this team to perform this action` | 0 | A team project's key whose creator is no longer a member of the team. |
| `slug has invalid format` | 0 | Not a full slug ending in a dash and a 5-character id. |
| `invalid json for contents param.` | 0 | Add or Update with `contents` that is not a JSON string. |
| `Contents do not match the expected workflow structure.` | 0 | A graph without the required shape (see [The Workflow Graph](#the-workflow-graph)). |
| `This tool in the workflow was not found: <slug>` | 0 | A step's model does not exist. |
| `Tags that start with wiro- are reserved for Wiro` | 0 | Add or Update with a `wiro-` tag. |
| `This workflow was modified by another user. Reload to see latest changes or save to overwrite.` | 0 | Update with an outdated `loadedUpdatetime`; the response adds `currentUpdatetime`. |
| `This workflow cannot be cloned` | 0 | Clone of a workflow that is not listed in the gallery. |
| `Unknown input field(s): <keys>. Check your workflow's Start Node schema for valid field names.` | 0 | Run with an input key the workflow does not have. |
| `A required input value is missing: <key>.` | 0 | Run without a value for a Start field a step needs. |
| `Workflows cannot include train tools as they take days to complete` | 0 | A step uses a training model. |
| `Insufficient balance` | 97 | The wallet holds less than $0.50 per model step that will run. |
| `You have reached your concurrent task limit...` | 96 | See [Concurrency Limits](/docs/concurrency-limits). |
| `Only people who can edit this workflow can stop a run at a step` | 0 | `breakpointNodeId` from someone who cannot edit the workflow. |
| `There is no workflow run yet.` | 0 | An unknown run token. |
| `Only a failed or stopped run can be resumed` | 0 | RunResume on a run that is running or completed. |

Authentication errors are listed in the [Error Reference](/docs/error-reference).
