# Agent Logs

Per-instance activity feed (tool calls, scheduled cron runs, message exchanges, and turn boundaries) for any deployed agent.

## Overview

Every Wiro agent appends one structured `ActivityEvent` JSON line per tool call, LLM turn boundary, scheduled task run and billed turn, plus each message that arrives on a connected Telegram, Slack or Discord channel. Secrets (matched by field name and by high-entropy value), internal tool-call IDs and API credentials are redacted before an event is written, so what shows up in `Logs` is safe to show end users.

A daily JSONL file is written for each calendar day; files older than 7 days are gzipped, files older than 180 days are deleted by the agent's daily maintenance cron.

The feed also lists what people and API keys did to the agent: starts and stops, renames, skill, connector and billing changes, connections, Screen views and Take Control sessions, browser resets, and deleted log days, each with who did it. These [who-did-what rows](#who-did-what-rows) don't depend on the agent running.

The endpoints below are **owner-or-team-admin** scoped. Plain members of the agent's team receive `useragent-team-admin-required` (code `97`); outside callers receive `useragent-access-denied`.

| Endpoint | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `POST /UserAgent/Logs` | Live tail (last N events for today, or a specific date). Poll it every 30 seconds or more. |
| `POST /UserAgent/LogsList` | List the days (`YYYY-MM-DD`) that have activity, with the size of each day's log. |
| `POST /UserAgent/LogsFile` | Read the **full** log of a specific date. |
| `POST /UserAgent/LogsDelete` | Delete the agent's own turns and tool calls for one date. Idempotent. |
| `POST /UserAgent/RunStreamToken` | Get a token for following the agent's Scheduled Tasks, background runs and model runs live on the [Agent WebSocket](/docs/agent-websocket#following-an-agents-background-runs), instead of polling `Logs`. |

> **Activity feed vs `Message/History`.** `Message/History` is a chat-bubble-level read of the conversation. `Logs` is a **runtime** view: every tool call, every turn and every scheduled task run. They serve different audiences (`Message/History` for end users, `Logs` for operators / power users).

## ActivityEvent Shape

Every event is a JSON object with this base shape:

```json
{
  "ts": "2026-05-03T14:00:10.234Z",
  "kind": "tool_completed",
  "tool": "web_fetch",
  "title": "Fetched https://blog.example.com/weekly-roundup-12",
  "summary": {
    "url": "https://blog.example.com/weekly-roundup-12",
    "status": 200,
    "bytes": 18432
  },
  "durationMs": 1840,
  "ok": true,
  "userUuid": "ada-uuid",
  "user": {
    "uuid": "ada-uuid",
    "firstname": "Ada",
    "lastname": "Lovelace",
    "email": "ada@example.com",
    "username": "ada",
    "avatar": "https://cdn.wiro.ai/avatars/ada.webp",
    "avatarinitials": "AL"
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `ts` | `string` | ISO-8601 UTC datetime when the event was recorded (e.g. `"2026-05-03T14:00:10.234Z"`). Parse with `Date.parse(ts)` for arithmetic. |
| `kind` | `string` | Fine-grained event class. One of: `"turn_started"`, `"turn_ended"` (an LLM turn boundary); `"tool_started"`, `"tool_completed"` (one pair per tool call); `"tool_blocked"` (a tool call the agent's safety rules refused); `"cron_finished"` (a scheduled task finished); `"user_message"` (a message received on a connected Telegram, Slack or Discord channel, not web chat); `"token_usage"` (a billed turn's token usage: chat / cron / voice post-call); `"token_usage_idempotent"` (a replayed usage report, already billed, informational only); `"media_relay"` (files from a reply were delivered); `"background_reply"` (a result that finished in the background was delivered to the chat). Rows about what was done to the agent have [`AGENT_*` kinds](#who-did-what-rows), and two note rows, `"runtime_log_unavailable"` and `"runtime_log_deleted"`, say what part of a day is missing. Show any kind you don't recognize by its `title`. |
| `tool` | `string?` | Present on `tool_started` / `tool_completed` / `tool_blocked`. The name of the tool the agent used. |
| `toolintegration` | `string?` | On `tool_started` and `tool_completed` when the step works in a connector: the connector's `slug`, for example `"wordpress"`, or a channel's key, such as `"telegram"`. Same closed list as on [timeline tool blocks](/docs/agent-messaging#tool-integration-and-action-values). |
| `toolaction` | `string?` | On `tool_started` and `tool_completed` when a word fits the step: what it does, for example `"click"`. Same closed list as on [timeline tool blocks](/docs/agent-messaging#tool-integration-and-action-values). Never set together with `toolintegration`. |
| `title` | `string` | Human-readable one-line description of what happened (e.g. `"Posted carousel: \"Brand voice teaser\""`, `"Fetched https://…"`, `"Token Usage"`). Always present. |
| `summary` | `object?` | Structured event-specific payload. Opaque on the wire, so render it as JSON when expanding the row. Secret values (`apikey`, `apppassword`, `clientsecret`, `bearer`, `token`, …) are masked before the event is written. Common keys: `file`, `method`, `host`, `path`, `preview`, `messageCount`, `jobId`, `status`, `reason`. |
| `durationMs` | `number?` | Wall-clock duration in milliseconds. Populated on `tool_completed`, `turn_ended`, `cron_finished` and `token_usage` events. |
| `ok` | `boolean?` | `true` for a successful completion, `false` for a failure. Populated on `tool_completed`, `turn_ended` and `cron_finished` events, and always `false` on `tool_blocked`. Pair with `error` for failure rows. It is always `true` on `AGENT_*` rows. A `turn_ended` for a turn the caller cancelled has no `ok`, and its title reads `Agent turn cancelled`. A `cron_finished` for a Scheduled Task run that the agent's spend limit or Model Access rule paused has no `ok` either, and its title starts with `Paused by a spend limit:` or `Paused by a Model Access rule:`. |
| `error` | `string?` | One-line failure message (when `ok: false`). |
| `cost` | `object?` | Legacy per-action charge, `{ credits, skill, action }`. Only events recorded before agents switched to per-turn token billing can carry it; current events never do. See the `token_usage` event for what a turn cost. |
| `userUuid` | `string?` | UUID of the actor who triggered the event. `"system"` for cron / internal events. May be missing on older rows, in which case the server falls back to the agent owner. |
| `user` | `object\|null` | Resolved actor: `{ uuid, firstname, lastname, email, username, avatar, avatarinitials }`. `null` when `userUuid` is `"system"` (automation / cron) or when the user record was deleted. |

> **What is `summary` for?** Tool events carry a short summary of the call: for example the file path for file tools, the program for `exec`, or the method, host and path for web requests. Turn events carry a short `preview` (plus `messageCount` on `turn_ended`); `cron_finished` carries `{ jobId, status }`, plus `reason` (`spend_limit` or `model_access`) when `status` is `paused`; `user_message` carries `{ preview }`; `tool_blocked` carries the `reason`. Treat the object as opaque and render-on-expand, since its shape depends on the tool and may change without a docs revision.

To tell what a tool call is doing, read `toolintegration` and `toolaction` instead of parsing `title` or `summary`. Both are missing when no word fits the step, and `tool_blocked` events don't carry them.

### Token-usage events

A `token_usage` event records the tokens and the AI usage of one billed turn: a chat reply, a cron run, or a voice post-call. A `token_usage_idempotent` event carries the **same shape** for a replayed usage callback that was already billed (informational; it does not deduct again). On top of the base `ActivityEvent` fields, these events add:

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `model` | `string` | Canonical model slug that served the turn (e.g. `"openai/gpt-5.4"`). |
| `tokens` | `object` | Nested token counts in **camelCase**: `{ input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite, total }` (each an integer). |
| `tokencost` | `number` | The turn's AI usage, in cents (`5` is $0.05). |
| `durationMs` | `number` | Wall-clock duration of the turn in milliseconds. |
| `calls` | `number` | Number of LLM calls made during the turn. |
| `remainingcredits` | `number` | Deprecated: kept for older readers and will be removed. Read the agent's AI usage and balance from `usage` on [`UserAgent/Detail`](/docs/agent-overview#usage-object). |

```json
{
  "ts": "2026-05-03T14:02:55.310Z",
  "kind": "token_usage",
  "title": "Token Usage",
  "model": "openai/gpt-5.4",
  "tokens": { "input": 3450, "output": 820, "cacheRead": 2400, "cacheWrite": 0, "total": 6670 },
  "tokencost": 5,
  "durationMs": 4200,
  "calls": 2,
  "userUuid": "system",
  "user": null
}
```

> **Nested vs flat token fields.** The activity-log `token_usage` event nests its counts in **camelCase** under `tokens.{input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite, total}`. `input` is uncached input and `total` is the exact sum of all four components. This is distinct from the **flat, lowercase** columns on message rows (`inputtokens`, `outputtokens`, `cachereadtokens`, …). Same underlying data, different shape.

> **AI usage vs. model runs.** An agent's own AI usage is counted once per LLM turn: each `token_usage` event is one billed turn, and its `tokencost` is in cents (`tokencost / 100` is the amount in USD). It comes from the plan's included usage first, then from the Wiro balance. A Wiro model the agent runs, for example for its video skill or through the `wiro` connector, is billed separately: Wiro charges it to the wallet of the workspace that owns the agent's Wiro API key at the model's usual price, passed through unchanged. That run shows up as an ordinary `tool_completed` event with no cost figure; its cost is the task's `totalcost` (see [Billing & Cost](/docs/tasks#task-billing)), and it is a `model-run` row in the agent's [Transactions](/docs/agent-transactions).

### Who-did-what rows

`Logs` and `LogsFile` also return what people and API keys did **to** the agent, and `LogsList` lists the days that have such rows. These rows sit in the same `events` list, in time order, with an `AGENT_*` value in `kind`. They come on top of the kinds above, which keep their meaning.

```json
{
  "ts": "2026-05-03T09:12:44.000Z",
  "kind": "AGENT_RENAMED",
  "title": "Agent renamed from \"Inbox Bot\" to \"Inbox Watcher\"",
  "ok": true,
  "summary": { "title": "Inbox Watcher", "previoustitle": "Inbox Bot", "fields": ["title"] },
  "userUuid": "ada-uuid",
  "user": {
    "uuid": "ada-uuid",
    "firstname": "Ada",
    "lastname": "Lovelace",
    "email": "ada@example.com",
    "username": "ada",
    "avatar": "https://cdn.wiro.ai/avatars/ada.webp",
    "avatarinitials": "AL"
  }
}
```

`title` is the line to show. `summary` holds the names and amounts behind it, never a connector value. `userUuid` and `user` name who did it. When an API key made the change, the title ends with `(API key "<project name>")` or `(via API key)`.

| `kind` | Example `title` |
|--------|-----------------|
| `AGENT_STARTED`, `AGENT_STOPPED`, `AGENT_RESTARTED` | `Agent started`, `Agent stopped`, `Agent restarted` |
| `AGENT_RENAMED` | `Agent renamed from "Inbox Bot" to "Inbox Watcher"` |
| `AGENT_UPDATED` | `Agent details updated: description, cover` |
| `AGENT_SETTINGS_UPDATED` | `Agent settings updated: timezone Europe/Istanbul`, `Agent settings updated: screen off` |
| `AGENT_TRANSFERRED` | `Agent moved to a team workspace`, `Agent moved to the personal workspace`; the system's rows when the agent's team or organization is deleted read `Agent moved to the personal workspace: its team was deleted` and `Agent moved to the personal workspace: its organization was deleted` |
| `AGENT_INSTRUCTION_ADDED`, `AGENT_INSTRUCTION_UPDATED`, `AGENT_INSTRUCTION_RENAMED`, `AGENT_INSTRUCTION_DELETED`, `AGENT_INSTRUCTION_REVERTED` | `Custom skill added: cs-brand-voice`, `Scheduled task updated: cs-cron-blog-scanner (text, schedule 0 9 * * 1)`, `Custom skill renamed: cs-brand-voice to cs-house-style`, `Scheduled task deleted: cs-cron-blog-scanner`, `Custom skill reverted to its preset: cs-brand-voice` |
| `AGENT_SKILLS_UPDATED` | `Skills updated: util-web-channel off` |
| `AGENT_CREDENTIAL_SAVED` | `Connector setting saved: wiro.apikey` |
| `AGENT_CREDENTIAL_REMOVED` | `Disconnected: wiro` (the agent's Wiro project was disconnected because the agent moved to a workspace the project isn't in, or because the project's team or organization was deleted) |
| `CONNECTOR_CONNECTED`, `CONNECTOR_DISCONNECTED` | `Connector connected: serper`, `Connector disconnected: serper` (see [Agent Connectors](/docs/agent-connectors)). When the agent moves to a workspace its Wiro project isn't in, or its Wiro project's team or organization is deleted, Wiro writes `Connector disconnected: wiro` with `summary.reason` `"workspace"` next to the `AGENT_CREDENTIAL_REMOVED` row (see [Moving the agent to another workspace](/docs/agent-connectors#moving-the-agent-to-another-workspace)) |
| `CONNECTOR_ACCOUNTS_SET` | `Connector accounts set: facebook-pages` |
| `CONNECTOR_REAUTH` | `Connector needs to be connected again: facebook-pages` (written by Wiro when a sign-in expired or was revoked) |
| `AGENT_PLAN_STARTED`, `AGENT_PLAN_RENEWED`, `AGENT_PLAN_CANCELLED`, `AGENT_PLAN_RESUMED` | `Starter plan started: $5.00 charged`, `Starter plan renewed: $5.00 charged`, `Plan cancelled, ends 2026-06-01`, `Plan cancellation undone` |
| `AGENT_PLAN_NOT_SAVED` | `Pro plan renewal did not finish: $24.00 charged`, `Max plan start did not finish: $100.00 charged` (the wallet paid and the plan could not be saved; see [Plan payments that did not finish](/docs/agent-transactions#plan-not-saved)) |
| `AGENT_TIER_UPGRADED` | `Plan upgraded from Starter to Pro; $12.50 charged` |
| `AGENT_PLAN_CHANGE_SCHEDULED`, `AGENT_PLAN_CHANGE_CANCELLED` | `Plan change scheduled: Pro to Starter on 2026-06-01`, `Scheduled plan change cancelled: stays on Pro` |
| `AGENT_PLAN_MOVE_SCHEDULED` | `Moves to the Starter plan ($5.00 a month) on 2026-06-01` (an agent subscribed before the three plans) |
| `AGENT_CREDITS_PURCHASED` | Older rows only: a pack bought before packs were retired, with what it cost |
| `AGENT_CHECKOUT_CREATED` | Older rows only: a card checkout link for a plan, from before plans moved to the balance |
| `AGENT_LOG_DAY_DELETED` | `Activity log day deleted: 2026-05-02` |
| `AGENT_SCREEN_VIEWED`, `AGENT_SCREEN_CONTROLLED` | `Watched the agent's screen`, `Took control of the agent's screen` |
| `AGENT_SCREEN_CONTROL_ENDED` | `Control of the agent's screen ended after 4 minutes 10 seconds: handed back` (`summary: { seconds, reason }`; see [Screen in the Activity Log](/docs/agent-overview#screen-in-the-activity-log)) |
| `AGENT_BROWSER_RESET` | `Agent browser reset` (see [Resetting the Browser](/docs/agent-overview#resetting-the-browser)) |
| `AGENT_DISK_ALMOST_FULL`, `AGENT_DISK_FULL` | `Disk almost full: 210 MB of 250 MB used.`, `Disk full: 260 MB of 250 MB used. The agent can't save new files until some are deleted.` (see [Disk Space](/docs/agent-overview#disk-space)) |
| `AGENT_DISK_TEMP_CLEARED`, `AGENT_DISK_HOST_RESTART` | `Temporary files passed 1 GB, so the agent restarted and cleared them.`, `The agent restarted to clear its temporary files.` (see [Disk Space](/docs/agent-overview#disk-space)) |

#### Note rows

Two more kinds say what part of a day is missing. They are notes, so they carry a `title` and no `ok`.

| `kind` | `title` | When |
|--------|---------|------|
| `runtime_log_unavailable` | `The agent's own turns and tool calls can be read while it runs` | The agent isn't running, so only its who-did-what rows are listed. |
| `runtime_log_unavailable` | `The agent's own turns and tool calls could not be read just now` | The agent's host did not answer. Read the day again later. |
| `runtime_log_deleted` | `The agent's own turns and tool calls for this day were deleted on 2026-05-04` | The day's log was deleted on a later day with `LogsDelete`. The day's who-did-what rows follow it. |

## **POST** /UserAgent/Logs

Live tail of the agent's activity feed. Returns the last N events for the requested date (defaults to today).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `useragentguid` | string | Yes | Your UserAgent instance guid. |
| `date` | string | No | `YYYY-MM-DD` to read a specific day's file. Default: today (UTC). |
| `lines` | number | No | Max events to return (max 5000). Default: `200`. |

**Polling:** leave 30 seconds or more between repeated polls.

##### Request

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.wiro.ai/v1/UserAgent/Logs" \
  -H "x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "useragentguid": "f8e7d6c5-b4a3-2190-fedc-ba0987654321", "lines": 200 }'
```

##### Response

```json
{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "date": "2026-05-03",
  "totalLines": 1428,
  "events": [
    {
      "ts": "2026-05-03T14:02:55.310Z",
      "kind": "token_usage",
      "title": "Token Usage",
      "model": "openai/gpt-5.4",
      "tokens": { "input": 3450, "output": 820, "cacheRead": 2400, "cacheWrite": 0, "total": 6670 },
      "tokencost": 5,
      "durationMs": 4200,
      "calls": 2,
      "userUuid": "system",
      "user": null
    },
    {
      "ts": "2026-05-03T14:02:54.902Z",
      "kind": "tool_completed",
      "tool": "exec",
      "toolintegration": "wiro",
      "title": "POST api.wiro.ai/v1/Run/google/nano-banana",
      "summary": {
        "method": "POST",
        "host": "api.wiro.ai",
        "path": "/v1/Run/google/nano-banana",
        "headers": ["Content-Type: application/json", "x-api-key: ***"],
        "body": { "prompt": "A paper boat on a calm lake at sunrise" }
      },
      "durationMs": 640,
      "ok": true,
      "userUuid": "system",
      "user": null
    },
    {
      "ts": "2026-05-03T14:00:10.305Z",
      "kind": "tool_completed",
      "tool": "exec",
      "title": "Posted: \"Weekly Roundup\"",
      "summary": {
        "title": "Weekly Roundup",
        "url": "https://blog.example.com/weekly-roundup-12",
        "categories": ["AI", "Tutorial"]
      },
      "durationMs": 1840,
      "ok": true,
      "userUuid": "system",
      "user": null
    },
    {
      "ts": "2026-05-03T13:30:00.000Z",
      "kind": "cron_finished",
      "title": "Cron ran: Scheduled Skill (cs-cron-blog-scanner)",
      "summary": { "jobId": "0f3c2a1b-7d4e-4c8f-9a6b-2e5d1c7f8a90", "status": "ok" },
      "durationMs": 4210,
      "ok": true,
      "userUuid": "system",
      "user": null
    },
    {
      "ts": "2026-05-03T13:14:42.118Z",
      "kind": "turn_ended",
      "title": "Agent turn completed",
      "summary": {
        "preview": "Here is this week's roundup draft…",
        "messageCount": 6
      },
      "durationMs": 8104,
      "ok": true,
      "userUuid": "ada-uuid",
      "user": {
        "uuid": "ada-uuid",
        "firstname": "Ada",
        "lastname": "Lovelace",
        "email": "ada@example.com",
        "username": "ada",
        "avatar": "https://cdn.wiro.ai/avatars/ada.webp",
        "avatarinitials": "AL"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> **About the `user` field.** Every event is decorated with the resolved actor: `{ uuid, firstname, lastname, email, username, avatar, avatarinitials }`.
>
> - An event with a user's `userUuid` carries that user's profile, or `null` when the user record was deleted.
> - An event triggered by **automation** has `userUuid: "system"` and `user: null`. That covers cron runs, the token usage of scheduled turns, and similar non-interactive writes (the system rows above).
> - An event without a `userUuid` (an incoming channel message, or a row older than user attribution) carries the agent owner's profile, so the row never shows an empty placeholder.

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `date` | `string\|null` | The actual date the events were read from (`YYYY-MM-DD`). |
| `totalLines` | `number` | Total rows for the day, who-did-what rows and notes included, whatever the `lines` cap. |
| `events` | `array<ActivityEvent>` | Newest first (descending by `ts`): `events[0]` is the most recent event; do not re-reverse. |

With a `lines` cap, older who-did-what rows of the day can take the place of the oldest agent events, up to half of the answer, so a stop from this morning stays in reach on a busy day. The answer stays within `lines`.

**Reading a stopped agent.** When the agent isn't running, or its host doesn't answer, `Logs` still answers `result: true` for a day with who-did-what rows. `events` starts with a `runtime_log_unavailable` note, followed by those rows, and `totalLines` counts the note:

```json
{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "date": "2026-05-03",
  "totalLines": 3,
  "events": [
    {
      "ts": "2026-05-03T16:20:11.000Z",
      "kind": "runtime_log_unavailable",
      "title": "The agent's own turns and tool calls can be read while it runs",
      "userUuid": "system",
      "user": null
    },
    {
      "ts": "2026-05-03T16:20:11.000Z",
      "kind": "AGENT_STOPPED",
      "title": "Agent stopped",
      "ok": true,
      "userUuid": "ada-uuid",
      "user": { "uuid": "ada-uuid", "firstname": "Ada", "lastname": "Lovelace" }
    },
    {
      "ts": "2026-05-03T09:12:44.000Z",
      "kind": "AGENT_CREDENTIAL_SAVED",
      "title": "Connector setting saved: wiro.apikey",
      "ok": true,
      "summary": { "fields": ["wiro.apikey"] },
      "userUuid": "ada-uuid",
      "user": { "uuid": "ada-uuid", "firstname": "Ada", "lastname": "Lovelace" }
    }
  ]
}
```

A day without such rows answers with one of the errors below.

## **POST** /UserAgent/LogsList

Returns the dates that have activity for this agent: days with a log file and days that only have who-did-what rows. Useful for rendering a date-picker.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `useragentguid` | string | Yes | Your UserAgent instance guid. |

##### Response

```json
{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "dates": [
    { "date": "2026-05-03", "sizeBytes": 184220, "compressed": false },
    { "date": "2026-05-02", "sizeBytes": 41280,  "compressed": true  },
    { "date": "2026-05-01", "sizeBytes": 0,      "compressed": false }
  ]
}
```

Each entry exposes `date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`, sorted newest-first), `sizeBytes` (raw byte size on disk; compressed size when `compressed: true`), and `compressed` (`true` once the day's log has been compressed to `<date>.jsonl.gz`; `false` for the active day's plain `.jsonl`). `sizeBytes` is `0` on a day with who-did-what rows and no log file, for example a day whose log was deleted. Reading either form via `LogsFile` returns the same decoded events. The host retains activity files for 180 days (rolling); older dates are removed and won't appear here.

**Reading a stopped agent.** When the agent isn't running, or its host doesn't answer, and it has who-did-what days, `LogsList` still answers `result: true` with those days and two more fields:

```json
{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "runtimeUnavailable": "not_running",
  "note": "The agent's own log days can be read while it runs, so this list may be missing days.",
  "dates": [
    { "date": "2026-05-03", "sizeBytes": null, "compressed": false },
    { "date": "2026-05-01", "sizeBytes": null, "compressed": false }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `runtimeUnavailable` | `string` | `"not_running"` or `"no_answer"`. Present only on this answer. |
| `note` | `string` | `The agent's own log days can be read while it runs, so this list may be missing days.` for `not_running`, `The agent's own log days could not be read just now, so this list may be missing days.` for `no_answer`. |
| `dates[].sizeBytes` | `null` | On this answer the size of a day isn't known. |

An agent with no who-did-what days answers with one of the errors below.

## **POST** /UserAgent/LogsFile

Reads the **full** log of a specific date and returns every event in it, who-did-what rows included. A stopped agent and a deleted day read as on `Logs`. Use this for "Download today's activity" buttons or for off-band analysis.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `useragentguid` | string | Yes | Your UserAgent instance guid. |
| `date` | string | Yes | `YYYY-MM-DD` of the file to read. |

##### Response

```json
{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "date": "2026-05-02",
  "truncated": false,
  "events": [
    {
      "ts": "2026-05-02T08:00:20.142Z",
      "kind": "turn_started",
      "title": "Agent turn started",
      "summary": { "preview": "Hi, can you draft a roundup post?" },
      "userUuid": "ada-uuid",
      "user": {
        "uuid": "ada-uuid",
        "firstname": "Ada",
        "lastname": "Lovelace",
        "email": "ada@example.com",
        "username": "ada",
        "avatar": "https://cdn.wiro.ai/avatars/ada.webp",
        "avatarinitials": "AL"
      }
    },
    {
      "ts": "2026-05-02T08:00:19.870Z",
      "kind": "user_message",
      "title": "User: Hi, can you draft a roundup post?",
      "summary": { "preview": "Hi, can you draft a roundup post?" },
      "user": {
        "uuid": "ada-uuid",
        "firstname": "Ada",
        "lastname": "Lovelace",
        "email": "ada@example.com",
        "username": "ada",
        "avatar": "https://cdn.wiro.ai/avatars/ada.webp",
        "avatarinitials": "AL"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Events are returned **newest first** (descending by `ts`), same as the live tail, so `events[0]` is the most recent; do not re-reverse. The `user` field follows the same resolution rules as the live tail above (see the `Logs` section's "About the `user` field" callout).

> **`truncated`** is `true` when the day's file is larger than 10 MiB. Only its newest 10 MiB of events are returned; older events of that day are not retrievable through this endpoint.

## **POST** /UserAgent/LogsDelete

Deletes the agent's own turns and tool calls for one date: its activity file and the gzipped sibling, if present. Who-did-what rows stay, so the date can stay in `LogsList` with `sizeBytes: 0`. The deletion adds an `AGENT_LOG_DAY_DELETED` row on the day you make it, and reads of an earlier day you deleted start with a `runtime_log_deleted` note that says when. Idempotent: deleting an already-gone date is a success no-op.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `useragentguid` | string | Yes | Your UserAgent instance guid. |
| `date` | string | Yes | `YYYY-MM-DD` of the day to delete. |

##### Response

```json
{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "date": "2026-05-01",
  "removed": { "plain": false, "gz": true }
}
```

`removed.{plain,gz}` reports which physical files were actually deleted. Both `false` is also a success (file was already gone).

## **POST** /UserAgent/RunStreamToken

Returns a token for following the agent's Scheduled Tasks, background runs and model runs live on the Agent WebSocket, so you see a run while it happens instead of polling `Logs`. Same access as `Logs`: the agent's owner and, on a team agent, the team's admins. A stopped agent gets a token too.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `useragentguid` | string | Yes | The guid of your deployed agent. |

##### Request

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.wiro.ai/v1/UserAgent/RunStreamToken" \
  -H "x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "useragentguid": "f8e7d6c5-b4a3-2190-fedc-ba0987654321" }'
```

##### Response

```json
{
  "result": true,
  "runstreamtoken": "Zr8Qm2Kx7VbN4tLpW1sYc9HdF6gJaE3uTo5iRk0nXqM",
  "expiresat": 1793664000,
  "errors": []
}
```

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `runstreamtoken` | string \| null | An opaque token valid until `expiresat`, 24 to 48 hours after it is issued. Send it in an `agent_run_subscribe` frame. `null` when the call fails. |
| `expiresat` | number \| null | Unix seconds when the token stops working, for example `1793664000`. `null` when the call fails. |

Keep the token private: whoever holds it can follow the agent's runs until `expiresat`. When less than 12 hours remain, call `RunStreamToken` again and subscribe with the new token. How to subscribe, the events, and the client rules are in [Following an agent's background runs](/docs/agent-websocket#following-an-agents-background-runs).

A failed call has one entry in `errors`:

```json
{
  "result": false,
  "runstreamtoken": null,
  "expiresat": null,
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 97,
      "message": "Only a team admin can perform this action on a team-owned agent.",
      "time": 1793491800
    }
  ]
}
```

| Error | Code | When |
|-------|------|------|
| `useragentguid is required` | 0 | `useragentguid` is missing or blank |
| `User agent not found` | 95 | Unknown guid, or the agent has been deleted |
| `You don't have access to this user agent` | 96 | The caller is neither the agent's owner nor on its team |
| `Only a team admin can perform this action on a team-owned agent.` | 97 | The caller is a plain member of the agent's team |
| `runstream-unavailable` | 0 | Following runs live is not available right now. Try again later |

## Usage Patterns

### Live polling for an in-app activity feed

Polling `Logs` every 30 seconds is the recommended cadence:

```javascript
async function pollActivity(useragentguid, onEvents) {
  let lastTs = 0;

  setInterval(async () => {
    const { data } = await axios.post(
      'https://api.wiro.ai/v1/UserAgent/Logs',
      { useragentguid, lines: 200 },
      { headers: { 'x-api-key': 'YOUR_API_KEY', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
    );

    const fresh = data.events.filter(e => Date.parse(e.ts) > lastTs);
    if (fresh.length === 0) return;

    onEvents(fresh);
    lastTs = Date.parse(fresh[0].ts);
  }, 30_000);
}
```

To show a Scheduled Task or another background run while it happens, follow the agent's [run stream](/docs/agent-websocket#following-an-agents-background-runs) and read `Logs` again when `agent_run_end` arrives.

### Daily download for off-band analysis

```bash
# 1) discover available dates
curl -X POST "https://api.wiro.ai/v1/UserAgent/LogsList" \
  -H "x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "useragentguid": "f8e7d6c5-b4a3-2190-fedc-ba0987654321" }'

# 2) download a specific date's full file
curl -X POST "https://api.wiro.ai/v1/UserAgent/LogsFile" \
  -H "x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "useragentguid": "f8e7d6c5-b4a3-2190-fedc-ba0987654321", "date": "2026-05-02" }' \
  > logs-2026-05-02.json
```

### Filtering server-side by `kind`

The endpoints don't support server-side filtering, so apply filters client-side:

```python
import requests

resp = requests.post(
    "https://api.wiro.ai/v1/UserAgent/LogsFile",
    headers={"x-api-key": "YOUR_API_KEY", "Content-Type": "application/json"},
    json={"useragentguid": "f8e7d6c5-b4a3-2190-fedc-ba0987654321", "date": "2026-05-02"}
).json()

cron_runs = [e for e in resp["events"] if e["kind"] == "cron_finished"]
print(f"{len(cron_runs)} cron runs on 2026-05-02")
for e in cron_runs:
    summary = e.get("summary") or {}
    print(f"  {e['title']} status={summary.get('status')}")
```

### Delete a day

`LogsDelete` removes the agent's own turns and tool calls for one day without waiting for the 180-day rotation. Who did what to the agent that day stays in the log:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.wiro.ai/v1/UserAgent/LogsDelete" \
  -H "x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "useragentguid": "f8e7d6c5-b4a3-2190-fedc-ba0987654321", "date": "2026-05-02" }'
```

## Errors

| Error | When |
|-------|------|
| `useragentguid is required` | Missing required parameter |
| `date is required` | `LogsFile` / `LogsDelete` without `date` |
| `useragent-access-denied` | Caller is neither the owner nor on the agent's team |
| `useragent-team-admin-required` | Caller is a member of the agent's team but not a team admin (code `97`) |
| `Agent is not assigned to a worker. It may not be running.` | The agent isn't running on a host (never started, stopped or being moved). Start it and retry |
| `Worker not found` | The agent's host is not available right now. Retry later |
| `Agent is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly.` | The agent's host did not answer (offline, network blip). Retry |
| `runstream-unavailable` | `RunStreamToken` only: following runs live is not available right now. Try again later |

`Logs`, `LogsFile` and `LogsList` answer with the last three errors only when there are no who-did-what rows to show. `LogsDelete` needs the agent on a host every time. `RunStreamToken` needs no host: a stopped agent gets a token too.

## Retention & Rotation

| Period | What happens |
|--------|--------------|
| Day 0-6 | File is plain JSONL (`YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl`). Live tail + LogsFile read it directly. |
| Day 7-180 | File is gzipped (`YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl.gz`). Reads are transparently decompressed; size in `LogsList` reports the on-disk compressed bytes. |
| Day 181+ | File is deleted by the agent's daily maintenance cron. `LogsList` no longer surfaces the date. |

Who-did-what rows are kept for the same 180 days.

> **Persistence is per-agent.** If Wiro re-allocates the agent's runtime (rare; happens during platform maintenance), the activity history starts fresh from that point. For long-term audit trails, schedule a daily `LogsFile` download to your own storage.

# Agent Use Cases

Build products with autonomous AI agents using the Wiro API.

## See These Use Cases on the Web

Wiro publishes interactive, fullscreen showcases for the most common agent use cases. Each one walks through a real product story end-to-end (build, deploy, daily operation, brand-voice authoring, scheduled autopilot, and a self-healing climax under an upstream API break), so you can see what the patterns below look like before writing any code.

| Showcase | What you'll see |
|----------|-----------------|

You can also browse every available pre-built agent at [wiro.ai/agents/browse](https://wiro.ai/agents/browse) (the visual mirror of [`POST /Agent/List`](/docs/agent-overview#post-agentlist)). Each agent template has its own marketing page at `wiro.ai/agents/{slug}` (for example [wiro.ai/agents/social-manager](https://wiro.ai/agents/social-manager), [wiro.ai/agents/voice-receptionist](https://wiro.ai/agents/voice-receptionist), or [wiro.ai/agents/blog-content-editor](https://wiro.ai/agents/blog-content-editor)) with screenshots, default skills, credential requirements, and live tier pricing. The full URL for each agent in the [Available Agents](#available-agents) table below is `https://wiro.ai/agents/{slug}`.

## Two Deployment Patterns

Every product built on Wiro agents follows one of two patterns. Choosing the right one depends on whether your users need to connect their own third-party accounts.

### Pattern 1: Instance Per Customer

Most agents interact with external services: posting to social media, managing ad campaigns, sending emails. These require OAuth tokens or API keys that belong to the end user. Deploy a **separate agent instance** for each of your customers.

**Why:** Each customer connects their own accounts. Credentials are bound to the instance, isolated from other customers. Each instance also has its own computer and browser, so the [Screen](/docs/agent-overview#screen-and-take-control) of a customer's agent shows only that customer's work.

**How:** Call `POST /UserAgent/Deploy` once per customer, then connect their accounts with [`ConnectorConnect`](/docs/agent-connectors#post-useragentconnectorconnect) on [Agent Connectors](/docs/agent-connectors).

#### Real-World Examples

| Your Product | Agent Type | Why Per-Customer |
|-------------|-----------|-----------------|
| Digital marketing agency dashboard | [Social Manager](https://wiro.ai/agents/social-manager) | Each client connects their own Twitter, Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, LinkedIn |
| Mobile app company | [App Review Support](https://wiro.ai/agents/app-review-support) | Each app has its own App Store / Google Play credentials |
| E-commerce platform | [Google Ads Manager](https://wiro.ai/agents/google-ads-manager) + [Meta Ads Manager](https://wiro.ai/agents/meta-ads-manager) | Each advertiser connects their own ad accounts |
| Marketing SaaS | [Newsletter Manager](https://wiro.ai/agents/newsletter-manager) | Each customer connects their own Brevo/SendGrid/Mailchimp |
| Sales platform | [Lead Generation Manager](https://wiro.ai/agents/lead-gen-manager) | Each sales team connects their own Apollo/Lemlist |
| Content agency tool | [Blog Content Editor](https://wiro.ai/agents/blog-content-editor) | Each client connects their own WordPress site |
| App publisher platform | [App Event Manager](https://wiro.ai/agents/app-event-manager) | Each app has its own App Store credentials |
| Mobile app publisher | [Push Notification Manager](https://wiro.ai/agents/push-notification-manager) | Each app has its own Firebase service account |
| Customer engagement tool | [Social Manager](https://wiro.ai/agents/social-manager) | Each brand manages their own social presence |
| Phone-receptionist platform for SMBs | [Voice Receptionist](https://wiro.ai/agents/voice-receptionist) | Each business has its own Twilio number, HubSpot CRM, and Google Calendar |
| Video marketing tool or agency | [Video Creator](https://wiro.ai/agents/video-creator) | Each client brings its own site, brand and test logins, and pays its model runs from its own Wiro project |

### Pattern 2: Session Per User

For conversational agents that don't need per-user credentials. One agent instance serves many users, each identified by a unique `sessionkey` that isolates their conversation history.

**Why:** No third-party accounts to connect. The agent answers questions using its built-in knowledge or pre-configured data sources.

**How:** Deploy one instance via `POST /UserAgent/Deploy`, then send messages with different `sessionkey` values per user. Deploy it with `"chatsetup": "off"`: your users' messages go out with your API key, which carries your rights, so with setup from chat on, a yes from one of them could change the agent's setup. See [Setup From Chat](/docs/agent-messaging#setup-from-chat). If you show the agent's Screen in your app, show it only to people who may see every user's work, or turn it off with `screen: "off"`: the agent's one computer shows all of their chats, and Take Control reaches every site its browser is signed in to (see [Screen in Your Own App](/docs/agent-overview#screen-in-your-own-app)).

**About `sessionkey`:** This field is optional. If omitted, messages go into a shared `"default"` session. Reuse the same `sessionkey` to continue a conversation (the agent retrieves prior messages as context). Use a fresh UUID to start a new conversation. The common convention is one `sessionkey` per end-user (e.g. `"user-456"`), but you can also use it per-thread (e.g. `"ticket-2025-0817"`) for products that group conversations by topic. See the [Agent Messaging](/docs/agent-messaging) guide for how sessions work. The session key is a label, not a WebSocket channel: you follow a turn with its `agenttoken` and a session with the `sessiontoken` from `Message/History` (see [Agent WebSocket](/docs/agent-websocket)).

#### Real-World Examples

| Your Product | Use Case | Why Sessions |
|-------------|---------|-------------|
| Knowledge base chatbot | Answer questions from documentation | No per-user credentials needed |
| Product recommendation advisor | Suggest products based on conversation | Same catalog for all users |
| Internal company assistant | HR policies, IT help, onboarding | Shared knowledge base |
| Customer support bot | Handle common support questions | No external service connections |

### When to Use Which

| Question | Instance Per Customer | Session Per User |
|---------|----------------------|-----------------|
| Does each user connect their own social/ad/email accounts? | Yes | No |
| Do credentials differ between users? | Yes | No |
| Is conversation the primary interaction? | Sometimes | Always |
| Does the agent perform actions on behalf of the user? | Yes | Rarely |
| How many instances do you need? | One per customer | One total (or a few) |

### Hybrid Pattern

A single product can combine both: a per-customer action agent plus a shared conversational agent sit side by side in the same frontend. For example:

- One **Social Manager** instance per customer (Pattern 1) to publish posts with their own connected social accounts (System User or OAuth, depending on the provider).
- One **shared knowledge-base chat** agent (Pattern 2) that answers product, billing, or onboarding questions across all customers, using `sessionkey` to keep each user's chat separate.

The two agents are independent deployments with different `useragentguid` values. Route user actions to the per-customer instance, and chat questions to the shared instance. Your backend decides which agent handles each request.

## Building Your Product

### White-Label Chat

Build a fully branded chat experience with no Wiro UI visible to your users.

The deploy flow has three stages: Deploy, Setup (only when the agent works with connectors or needs credentials), and Start.

1. **Deploy** an agent via `POST /UserAgent/Deploy`: returns `useragents[0].guid` and starts the instance in `status: 6` (setup-required). A prepaid Deploy then queues it (`status: 2`) once its subscription is provisioned. Send `"chatsetup": "off"` too, so your users' messages can't change the agent's setup; make setup changes from your own backend.
2. **Setup** the connectors and credentials (only if the agent template needs them): connect the services it works with through [Agent Connectors](/docs/agent-connectors) (`POST /UserAgent/ConnectorConnect`, with fields or the vendor's sign-in; the template's `suggestedconnectors` on [`Agent/Detail`](/docs/agent-overview#post-agentdetail) lists them), and save channels with `POST /UserAgent/CredentialUpsert` and the Wiro project with `POST /UserAgent/CredentialProjectBind` (see [Agent Credentials](/docs/agent-credentials)). These calls don't change `status`: on an agent still at `status: 6`, call `POST /UserAgent/Update` with `{ "guid": "<useragent-guid>" }` after the last one and check `setuprequired` on its response. While it's `true`, the agent cannot start. Once all required credentials are set up, that call flips `setuprequired` to `false` and `status` to `0`; connectors never hold an agent at `status: 6`. For Pattern 2 (knowledge-base / chat-only agents) there is nothing to set up, so this stage is skipped and the agent is ready to start right after Deploy.
3. **Start**: a prepaid Deploy already queued the agent, and it goes through `status: 3` (starting) → `status: 4` (running). Call `POST /UserAgent/Start` when it is stopped (`status: 0`, for example after `Update` moved it out of `status: 6`) or errored (`status: 5`).
4. Build your own chat UI.
5. Send messages via `POST /UserAgent/Message/Send`.
6. Stream responses in real-time via [Agent WebSocket](/docs/agent-websocket) using the `agenttoken`.
7. Manage conversation history with `POST /UserAgent/Message/History`.

See [Agent Overview](/docs/agent-overview) for the full lifecycle state table (`status: 0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6`).

To let the people who manage an agent set it up from your chat, with setup cards, connect steps and restarts shown in your own UI, keep `chatsetup` at `"all"` and follow [Agent Chat Integration](/docs/agent-chat-integration).

To show the agent's live Screen in your UI, with Take Control for the people you choose, see [Screen and Take Control in Your App](/docs/agent-chat-integration#screen-and-take-control-in-your-app).

```bash
# Deploy — prepaid + tier are required (the plan is paid from your Wiro balance)
curl -X POST "https://api.wiro.ai/v1/UserAgent/Deploy" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -d '{
    "agentguid": "agent-template-guid",
    "title": "Customer Support Bot",
    "useprepaid": true,
    "tier": "starter",
    "chatsetup": "off"
  }'

# Pattern 1 only — fill any missing credentials, then verify setuprequired flipped to false
curl -X POST "https://api.wiro.ai/v1/UserAgent/Detail" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -d '{ "guid": "deployed-useragent-guid" }'

# Start the agent when it is stopped (status 0) or errored (status 5): a prepaid Deploy already queues it
curl -X POST "https://api.wiro.ai/v1/UserAgent/Start" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -d '{ "guid": "deployed-useragent-guid" }'

# Send a message
curl -X POST "https://api.wiro.ai/v1/UserAgent/Message/Send" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -d '{
    "useragentguid": "deployed-useragent-guid",
    "message": "How do I reset my password?",
    "sessionkey": "user-456"
  }'
```

### Webhook-Driven Pipelines

For backend-to-backend integrations where you don't need real-time streaming.

1. Send a message with a `callbackurl`
2. Continue processing other work
3. Receive the agent's response via HTTP POST to your webhook endpoint
4. Chain the result into your next workflow step

See [Agent Webhooks](/docs/agent-webhooks) for payload format and retry policy.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.wiro.ai/v1/UserAgent/Message/Send" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -d '{
    "useragentguid": "deployed-useragent-guid",
    "message": "Generate a weekly performance report",
    "sessionkey": "pipeline-run-789",
    "callbackurl": "https://your-server.com/webhooks/report-ready"
  }'
```

### Generative Media Studio

A richer variant of white-label chat: besides replying with text, the agent **generates images, video, or audio** through Wiro AI models and streams them into a live activity feed beside the conversation. This is the pattern behind Wiro's own Studio. It layers the realtime socket on top of the **Session-Per-User** model.

**Shape:**

- One deployed agent whose Wiro project is set to your project (see [The agent's Wiro project](/docs/agent-credentials#the-agents-wiro-project)). Media the agent generates is billed to the wallet of the workspace that owns that project (your personal wallet, or the team wallet for a team project). The agent runs models with that project's key from its skills, or with the tools of the `wiro` connector (see [The Wiro connector](/docs/agent-connectors#the-wiro-connector)).
- One `sessionkey` per end user (Pattern 2 above): the same agent instance serves everyone, and each user's chat history is isolated by session. The agent's model runs are not: with the `wiro` connector, each user can reach the runs the agent made for the others (see [The Wiro connector](/docs/agent-connectors#the-wiro-connector)).
- A single WebSocket connection carries three things at once: the streaming chat reply, the per-turn token-usage report, and discovery of any model runs the agent launches.

**End-to-end sequence an integrator replicates:**

1. **Deploy once** (prepaid): `POST /UserAgent/Deploy` with `useprepaid: true` + `tier`. Connect the agent's Wiro project with `POST /UserAgent/CredentialProjectBind`, then `Start`.
2. **Open the socket**: connect to `wss://socket.wiro.ai/v1` and wait for the `connected` frame.
3. **(Optional) name the session**: `POST /UserAgent/Message/RenameSession` seeds a titled, empty session that shows up immediately in `Message/Sessions`.
4. **Send a message**: `POST /UserAgent/Message/Send` with the user's `sessionkey`. Subscribe `{ "type": "agent_info", "agenttoken": "<agenttoken-from-send>" }` and stream `agent_start → agent_output × N → agent_end`.
5. **Patch token usage**: ~250-500 ms after `agent_end`, an `agent_usage_report` frame delivers the turn's token counts and `tokencost` (in cents); splice them onto the message by `messageguid`.
6. **Collect generated media**: when the agent runs a model, an `agent_wiroai_runtask` frame arrives on the same `agenttoken` with a `socketaccesstoken`. Subscribe to it with `{ "type": "task_info", "tasktoken": "<socketaccesstoken>" }` and stream `task_queue → task_start → task_output → task_postprocess_end`; the final frame carries the output media URLs. See [Agent WebSocket → Model runs the agent triggers](/docs/agent-websocket#model-runs-the-agent-triggers).
7. **Manage sessions**: list with `Message/Sessions`, rename with `Message/RenameSession`, clear/forget with `Message/DeleteSession` (`rotate: true` to wipe the agent's memory of the thread).

Either deployment shape works: run **one** media agent and separate users by `sessionkey`, or deploy **separate** agents per workspace/customer. Both use the exact same socket and messaging surface. Share one media agent only among users who may see each other's media; otherwise deploy one agent per customer.

### Scheduled Automation

Combine agents with cron jobs for recurring tasks.

```
Cron (every Monday 9am)
  → POST /UserAgent/Message/Send (with callbackurl)
    → Agent processes the task
      → Webhook fires to your server
        → Your server emails the report / posts to Slack / updates dashboard
```

This pattern works well for weekly social media content planning, daily ad performance reviews, monthly newsletter generation, and automated lead enrichment pipelines.

### Multi-Agent Orchestration

Deploy multiple specialized agents and coordinate them from your backend.

```
Your Backend
  ├── Research Agent → "Find trending topics in AI this week"
  │     ↓ webhook response
  ├── Writing Agent → "Write a blog post about: {research results}"
  │     ↓ webhook response
  └── Publishing Agent → "Publish this post to WordPress and share on social media"
```

Each agent is an independent instance with its own credentials. Your backend passes output from one agent as input to the next.

## Available Agents

Wiro provides pre-built agent templates you can deploy immediately. Each agent specializes in a specific domain and comes with the relevant skills. It suggests the connectors it works with (`suggestedconnectors` on [`Agent/Detail`](/docs/agent-overview#post-agentdetail)), and you connect them after you deploy it.

| Agent | What It Does | Connectors |
|-------|-------------|-------------|
| **[Social Manager](https://wiro.ai/agents/social-manager)** | Create, schedule, and publish social media content | Twitter/X, TikTok, LinkedIn (OAuth); Instagram and Facebook Pages (System User recommended or own OAuth) |
| **[Blog Content Editor](https://wiro.ai/agents/blog-content-editor)** | Write and publish blog posts (WordPress draft + publish workflow) | WordPress (App Password), Gmail (optional, for inbox requests) |
| **[Google Ads Manager](https://wiro.ai/agents/google-ads-manager)** | Create and optimize Google Ads campaigns, daily performance reports | Google Ads (OAuth), Calendarific (API key), Google Drive (optional, Service Account) |
| **[Meta Ads Manager](https://wiro.ai/agents/meta-ads-manager)** | Manage Facebook and Instagram ad campaigns, audience analysis | Meta Ads (System User recommended or own OAuth), Calendarific (API key), Google Drive (optional, Service Account) |
| **[Newsletter Manager](https://wiro.ai/agents/newsletter-manager)** | Design and send email newsletters to subscriber lists | Brevo, SendGrid, Mailchimp, HubSpot (any one, API key or OAuth) |
| **[Lead Generation Manager](https://wiro.ai/agents/lead-gen-manager)** | Find and enrich leads, run multi-channel outreach, analyze replies | Apollo (API key), Lemlist (API key), HubSpot (optional, for CRM sync) |
| **[App Review Support](https://wiro.ai/agents/app-review-support)** | Monitor app store reviews, draft responses in operator's tone | App Store Connect (private key JWT), Google Play (service account) |
| **[App Event Manager](https://wiro.ai/agents/app-event-manager)** | Scan global holidays, suggest and create App Store + Google Play in-app events | App Store Connect (JWT), Google Play (service account), Calendarific (API key) |
| **[Push Notification Manager](https://wiro.ai/agents/push-notification-manager)** | Craft locale- and timezone-aware push notifications, queue dispatch | Firebase (service account JSON per app), Calendarific (API key) |
| **[Voice Receptionist](https://wiro.ai/agents/voice-receptionist)** | Answer phone calls 24/7 with a real-time AI receptionist: recognises callers from CRM, books from your calendar, drafts CRM notes + follow-up emails, streams a live transcript to chat | Twilio Voice (Account SID, Auth Token, phone number) for inbound phone; HubSpot (optional, caller recognition); Google Calendar (optional, slot lookup); Google Drive (optional); Brevo or HubSpot (any one, optional, follow-up email drafts); Telegram bot (optional, operator approvals) |
| **[Video Creator](https://wiro.ai/agents/video-creator)** | Turn a website, web app, store listing, document or product photos into a share-ready video with real screens, voice-over, music and captions | Wiro project (the video's model runs are billed to its wallet); the [YouTube](https://wiro.ai/connectors/youtube) and [Instagram](https://wiro.ai/connectors/instagram) connectors (optional, to publish finished videos); Telegram bot (optional) |

> The list above matches the agent templates currently deployed in production. The exact set evolves over time as new templates ship, so fetch `POST /Agent/List` for the live catalog. Each agent's full marketing page lives at `https://wiro.ai/agents/{slug}` (linked in the first column).

### Deploying an Agent

```python
import requests

headers = {
    "x-api-key": "YOUR_API_KEY",
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
}

# List available agents
agents = requests.post(
    "https://api.wiro.ai/v1/Agent/List",
    headers=headers,
    json={}
)
print(agents.json())

# Deploy an instance (always prepaid — the plan is paid from your Wiro balance)
deploy = requests.post(
    "https://api.wiro.ai/v1/UserAgent/Deploy",
    headers=headers,
    json={
        "agentguid": "social-manager-agent-guid",
        "title": "Acme Corp Social Media",
        "useprepaid": True,
        "tier": "starter"
    }
)
useragent_guid = deploy.json()["useragents"][0]["guid"]

# Connect X with your own X app (see Agent Connectors)
connect = requests.post(
    "https://api.wiro.ai/v1/UserAgent/ConnectorConnect",
    headers=headers,
    json={
        "useragentguid": useragent_guid,
        "slug": "twitter",
        "values": {"clientid": "YOUR_X_CLIENT_ID", "clientsecret": "YOUR_X_CLIENT_SECRET"},
        "redirecturl": "https://your-app.com/settings?slug=twitter"
    }
)
authorize_url = connect.json()["authorizeUrl"]
# Redirect your user to authorize_url

# A prepaid Deploy already queued the agent: start it only when it is stopped (0) or errored (5)
instance = requests.post(
    "https://api.wiro.ai/v1/UserAgent/Detail",
    headers=headers,
    json={"guid": useragent_guid}
).json()
if instance["useragents"][0]["status"] in (0, 5):
    requests.post(
        "https://api.wiro.ai/v1/UserAgent/Start",
        headers=headers,
        json={"guid": useragent_guid}
    )

# Send a message
message = requests.post(
    "https://api.wiro.ai/v1/UserAgent/Message/Send",
    headers=headers,
    json={
        "useragentguid": useragent_guid,
        "message": "Create a thread about our new product launch",
        "sessionkey": "campaign-q2"
    }
)
print(message.json())
```

Browse available agents and their capabilities via [POST /Agent/List](/docs/agent-overview#post-agentlist) or in the [Wiro dashboard](https://wiro.ai/agents).

# Organizations & Teams

Collaborate with your team under a shared workspace with unified billing, access controls, and resource management.

## Overview

Wiro supports three workspace contexts for organizing your resources:

- **Personal**: your default workspace. Projects, agents, and wallet are tied to your individual account.
- **Organization**: a parent entity that groups one or more teams. The organization owner controls the lifecycle of teams and their members.
- **Team**: a workspace under an organization with its own wallet, projects, agents, and member permissions. Team members share access to resources deployed within the team.

```
Personal Account
├── Personal Projects
├── Personal Agents
└── Personal Wallet

Organization (created by you)
├── Team A
│   ├── Team Wallet
│   ├── Team Projects
│   ├── Team Agents
│   └── Members (admins, members)
├── Team B
│   ├── Team Wallet
│   ├── Team Projects
│   ├── Team Agents
│   └── Members
└── ...
```

Every user always has a personal workspace. Organizations and teams are optional: you can use Wiro entirely in personal mode without ever creating an organization.

## Key Concepts

### Workspaces and Context

When you make an API request or use the dashboard, you operate in one of two contexts:

| Context | Resources you see | Wallet charged | How to activate |
|---------|-------------------|----------------|-----------------|
| **Personal** | Your personal projects, agents, tasks | Your personal wallet | Default. In the dashboard, choose Personal with **Switch Workspace** (or **Switch to Personal** on the Organizations page); in the API, use a personal project API key |
| **Team** | Team projects, team agents, team tasks | Team wallet | In the dashboard, choose the team with **Switch Workspace** (or **Switch** on the Organizations page); in the API, use a team project API key |

Switching context changes which projects, agents, and wallet you interact with. Resources in one context are isolated from the other: personal agents cannot see team projects, and team agents cannot access personal resources.

### Resource Isolation

Each workspace is fully isolated:

- **Projects** belong to either your personal workspace or a specific team. A project's API key automatically resolves the correct context.
- **Agents** are deployed into a workspace. Team agents are visible to all team members; personal agents are visible only to you.
- **Wallet transactions** are recorded against the workspace that initiated them. Team tasks deduct from the team wallet; personal tasks deduct from your personal wallet.
- **Tasks** are tagged with the workspace context and only appear in the matching project usage and statistics views.

### Transferring Resources

Projects and agents can be transferred between workspaces:

- **Personal → Team**: move a project or agent from your personal workspace into a team you have admin access to
- **Team → Personal**: move a project you created, or an agent you deployed, from a team you have admin access to back to your personal workspace. Only the original creator or deployer can do this.
- **Team → Team**: move a project or agent between teams you have admin access to in the same or different organizations

When a resource is transferred, its billing context changes immediately. Future tasks on a transferred project will be billed to the new workspace's wallet. Transfer operations are available in the dashboard and via the API. An agent that has been in a team doesn't get [Take Control](/docs/agent-overview#take-control) after it moves back to a personal workspace until its owner [resets its browser](/docs/agent-overview#resetting-the-browser): the browser may still hold team members' sign-ins.

> **Important:** Agents can only access projects in the same workspace. If you transfer a project out of a team, agents in that team can no longer use it.

## Organizations vs Teams

An **organization** is a management container: it does not hold resources directly. All resources (projects, agents, wallets) live inside **teams**.

| Feature | Organization | Team |
|---------|-------------|------|
| Holds projects and agents | No | Yes |
| Has a wallet | No | Yes |
| Has members | No (members belong to teams) | Yes |
| Can be created by | Any user | Organization owner |
| Can be deleted by | Organization owner | Organization owner |
| Can be restored | Yes, by the owner | No separate restore. Teams archived when their organization was deleted come back when it is restored |

Restoring an organization does not move projects or agents back into its teams. They stay in the personal workspaces of the people who created or deployed them until transferred back.

A single user can own multiple organizations, and each organization can contain multiple teams.

## Roles

| Role | Scope | Permissions |
|------|-------|-------------|
| **Owner** | Organization | Create and remove teams; edit, remove, and restore the organization. The owner is added as an admin of every team they create and can't be demoted to member, so they also have all Admin permissions there |
| **Admin** | Team | Edit team settings (name and description); set the team's spend limits, member limits included, and its Model Access rules; invite members and cancel invitations; change roles; remove members; deploy and manage team agents; edit and delete team projects; transfer agents, projects, and credit; redeem coupons into the team wallet; set up, change, and turn off the team wallet's auto-pay |
| **Member** | Team | Run models and create projects in the team workspace (billed to the team wallet), chat with team agents, and view the member list, the team's spend limits and Model Access rules, and every member's spending |

The organization creator is automatically the owner. When the owner creates a team, including the Default Team created with the organization, they are added to it as an admin member. Additional members are invited by email and join once they accept the invitation, signed in with the invited email address, within 72 hours.

On a team agent whose Chat Mode is `"collaborative"`, the team's admins and the agent's owner can watch its [Screen](/docs/agent-overview#screen-and-take-control) in the Wiro panel, and an app can show it through a team project's API key that one of them created; other members can't. Nobody can take control of a team agent's computer.

## Getting Started

1. **Create an organization**: go to your [Dashboard](https://wiro.ai/panel/organization) and click "Create Organization". A team named "Default Team" is created automatically, with you as its admin.
2. **Add more teams (optional)**: as the organization owner, click "Create Team" on the organization card to add another team, for example one per project
3. **Invite members**: send email invitations to your teammates
4. **Fund the team wallet**: switch to the team workspace and add credit. Admins and the owner can also move credit from their personal wallet with **Transfer Credit** and redeem coupons into the team wallet
5. **Create projects**: with the team workspace selected, create API projects. Their API keys run models on the team wallet
6. **Deploy agents**: team admins can deploy agent instances within the team for shared access

For step-by-step instructions, see [Managing Teams](/docs/organizations-managing-teams).

## What's Next

- [Managing Teams](/docs/organizations-managing-teams): Create organizations, invite members, manage roles and permissions
- [Team Billing & Spending](/docs/organizations-billing): Wallets, spend limits and their alert emails, and Model Access rules
- [Team API Access](/docs/organizations-api-access): How workspace context works with API keys and context guards
